items.title: Injectable bioactive glass hydrogels orchestrate metalloimmunotherapy by depleting pathogenic B cells and rescuing bone in rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is characterized by persistent synovial inflammation and progressive bone destruction. Transcriptomic profiling identified hyperactivated B cells as key contributors to osteoimmune dysregulation, supporting localized B cell intervention as a therapeutic strategy. Here, an injectable thermosensitive hydroxypropyl chitin hydrogel incorporating Cu/Zn-doped bioactive glass particles, termed BG@HPCH, was developed for localized metalloimmunotherapy. BG incorporation improved the shear-thinning behavior, thermosensitive gelation, storage modulus, and stability of the hydrogel. In vitro, ionic release from BG@HPCH selectively reduced pathogenic B cell survival while preserving mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) viability. The optimized M-BG@HPCH increased the B cell dead-cell area from 1.93 ± 0.48% to 91.12 ± 0.90% at 24 h, while maintaining MSC viability at 98.59 ± 0.26% after 3 days. In TNF-transgenic mice, a single intra-articular injection of BG@HPCH reduced arthritis index scores from 2.88 ± 0.18 to 1.81 ± 0.13 at day 28, limited bone erosion, and showed no detectable systemic toxicity. Micro-CT analysis showed improved bone preservation, with BV/TV increasing from 30.00 ± 6.74% to 55.66 ± 1.07%. OCN staining further confirmed enhanced osteogenic activity, with the OCN + area increasing by 2.16 times. Flow cytometry confirmed reduced B220 + CD45.2 + B cell accumulation in treated joints. Single-cell RNA sequencing of 23,921 joint cells showed that BG@HPCH reduced inflammatory B cell, macrophage, and fibroblast subsets while expanding osteoblast-associated regenerative populations, accompanied by suppression of CD23 -  and CD74-associated B cell signaling axes. These findings establish BG@HPCH as a localized immunoregenerative biomaterial for coordinating pathogenic B cell depletion and bone repair in RA.

items.title: Adult-onset chronic nonbacterial osteitis mimicking refractory axial psoriatic arthritis: successful treatment with combined IL-1/IL-17 inhibition: a case report and brief literature review.
items.abstract: We report a 46-year-old man with palmoplantar pustular psoriasis and severe axial inflammation who was initially diagnosed with refractory axial psoriatic arthritis. Despite sequential treatment with multiple biologic and targeted therapies, disease activity persisted. Reassessment based on anterior chest wall involvement, characteristic positron emission tomography/computed tomography findings, human leukocyte antigen B27 negativity, and exclusion of infectious, malignant, and monogenic autoinflammatory disorders supported a diagnosis of adult-onset chronic nonbacterial osteitis (CNO). The patient showed a marked clinical, laboratory, and imaging response to interleukin (IL)-1 blockade, and sustained disease control was achieved with combined IL-1/IL-17 inhibition. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of adult CNO and suggests a potential role for dual cytokine inhibition in refractory disease. A brief literature review on current treatment options is provided.

items.title: Distinct tear cytokine profile and ocular surface phenotype in primary biliary cholangitis patients with Sjögren's syndrome.
items.abstract: To compare the ocular surface phenotype and tear cytokine profile of primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) patients with and without concomitant Sjögren's syndrome (SS). This case-control study enrolled 21 PBC patients with SS (PBC-SS group), 23 PBC patients without SS (PBC-only group), and 20 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. All participants underwent standardized ocular surface assessments including Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI) questionnaire, lipid layer thickness (LLT), incomplete blink rate, tear meniscus height (TMH), non-invasive tear film breakup time (NIBUT), meibomian gland loss (MGL), Schirmer I test, and corneal fluorescein staining (CFS). Tear concentrations of six cytokines [interleukin (IL)-6, IL-8, IL-10, vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1), vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF)] were measured using a customized ultra-sensitive quantitative antibody array (QAA-CUST) platform. The three groups were comparable in terms of age (54.2±8.6, 52.8±9.3, and 53.5±8.9y, respectively; P =0.873) and gender distribution (female predominance: 100%, 91.3%, and 95%; P =0.412). Compared to PBC-only patients, the PBC-SS group exhibited significantly worse ocular surface parameters, including higher OSDI scores (45.6±12.3 vs 28.4±9.7), lower Schirmer I values (3.8±2.1 vs 7.6±3.2 mm/5min), reduced TMH (0.18±0.06 vs 0.22±0.05 mm), and shorter NIBUT (4.2±1.8 vs 6.2±2.0s), all P <0.001. Both PBC groups showed reduced LLT and increased MGL compared to healthy controls ( P <0.05), while CFS scores were similarly elevated in both PBC groups versus controls ( P <0.001). Tear cytokine analysis revealed significantly higher levels of IL-6, IL-8, and VCAM-1, and lower levels of IL-10 in the PBC-SS group compared to the PBC-only group (all P <0.05). VEGF was elevated in both PBC groups versus controls ( P <0.05). In PBC-SS patients, VCAM-1 demonstrated the strongest correlations with Schirmer I values ( ρ =-0.71, P <0.001) and CFS scores ( ρ =0.68, P <0.001). Compared to PBC-only patients, PBC patients with SS exhibit a distinct and more severe ocular surface phenotype characterized by pronounced aqueous tear deficiency and a unique tear inflammatory signature with elevated VCAM-1, IL-6, IL-8 and reduced IL-10. Tear cytokine profiling, particularly VCAM-1, may serve as a valuable non-invasive tool for identifying SS comorbidity in PBC patients and monitoring disease severity.

items.title: Evaluation of A Novel Point-of-Care Real-Time PCR Platform for Rapid Screening of HLA-B27 Using Whole Blood.
items.abstract: HLA-B27 positivity is a key determinant for early referral of axial spondyloarthropathies, yet timely testing remains constrained by reliance on centralised molecular laboratories requiring substantial infrastructure and specialised personnel. We developed and validated a fully automated, cartridge-based real-time PCR point-of-care platform, the MoiM HLA-B27 Detection Kit run on the MoiM Dx100 analyser, which integrates sample loading, magnetic bead-based DNA extraction, and qPCR into a single disposable cartridge for sample-to-answer testing directly from whole blood. Analytical performance was characterised for extraction efficiency, limit of detection, and specificity using the UCLA Immunogenetics Center DNA Reference Panel, and clinical performance was evaluated in 217 whole blood specimens submitted for routine HLA-B27 genotyping, compared against a reference PCR sequence-specific primer (PCR-SSP) method with discordant cases arbitrated by Luminex PCR-SSOP. The platform produced DNA of purity comparable to manual extraction (mean A260/A280 1.9 ± 0.04), with 100% analytical specificity and no cross-reactivity against B7-related cross-reactive group alleles. Optimising the cycle threshold cut-off eliminated non-specific late-cycle amplification responsible for four initial false positives. In the final clinical cohort (67 positive, 150 negative), the assay achieved 100% concordance with PCR-SSP (sensitivity 100% [95% CI 94.6-100%]; specificity 100% [95% CI 97.6%-100%]; Cohen's κ = 1.00), with shorter hands-on time, faster turnaround, and lower per-test cost. This integrated platform delivers laboratory-grade HLA-B27 results in a rapid, accessible format that may shorten the diagnostic pathway for ankylosing spondylitis and related spondyloarthropathies.

items.title: Additional B-Lymphocyte Stimulator Inhibitors Treatment Facilitated Glucocorticoid Withdrawal in Lupus Nephritis Patients: A Real-World Retrospective Observational Single-Center Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Glucocorticoid (GC) withdrawal remains a major challenge for lupus nephritis (LN). In this 20-year retrospective cohort, we evaluated whether B-lymphocyte stimulator (BLyS) inhibitors facilitated GC discontinuation. Among 702 LN patients, 553 were treated with standard-of-care alone, and 149 received add-on BLyS inhibitors (belimumab or telitacicept). Patients receiving BLyS inhibitors achieved a higher rate of GC withdrawal than those receiving standard-of-care alone (10.7% vs. 5.61%, p = 0.026). Kaplan-Meier analysis confirmed a higher cumulative incidence of GC withdrawal in the BLyS inhibitor group ( p = 0.001). After adjusting for age, sex, Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Disease Activity Index, acute kidney injury, nephrotic syndrome, and renal histopathology, time-dependent Cox regression revealed that BLyS inhibitor therapy was independently associated with a higher GC withdrawal rate (hazard ratio [HR] = 7.97, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 4.11-15.5, p  < 0.001). Exploratory subgroup analyses indicated that among GC‑discontinued patients, Class IV LN predominated in the BLyS inhibitor group, whereas Class V LN was more prevalent in controls. During follow-up, no renal flares occurred in BLyS inhibitor-treated patients who discontinued GCs, though there was no significant between-group difference. In conclusion, add-on BLyS inhibitor therapy may serve as a potential steroid withdrawal-permissive approach for LN, pending further prospective validation of its clinical applicability.

items.title: Adapting an Interprofessional Medication Adherence Program for Gout (IMAP-Gout): A Theory-Informed Pre-Implementation Analysis Using the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF).
items.abstract: Adherence rates to urate lowering therapy in gout remain low. Successfully implemented in Switzerland, the Interprofessional Medication Adherence Program (IMAP) supports medication adherence through an ambulatory-based model of care that includes pharmacists, motivational interviewing, and electronic adherence monitoring. We aimed to determine the facilitators and barriers to implementing IMAP for patients with gout in a hospital in Australia. Multi-stakeholder, semi-structured interviews were analyzed using the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF) for each stakeholder group and Implementation Mapping was used to identify target behaviors. A total of 51 interviews were conducted with patients (n = 8), a general practitioner (n = 1), pharmacists (n = 8), rheumatologists (n = 21), nurses (n = 4), and decision/policy makers (n = 9). Patients identified their health-reducing gout flares and improving function-as key facilitators, while barriers included environmental context and resources, such as time constraints. Pharmacists and nurses were motivated by professional role and identity, particularly the opportunity to extend their skillsets. However, pharmacists faced barriers related to environmental context and resources, including insufficient funding or managerial support. Nurses were keen to improve their knowledge and skills, such as training in motivational interviewing. Rheumatologists were driven by their goals of improving patient outcomes, but expressed concerns about ensuring governance over a pharmacist-led program. For general practitioners, behaviors were facilitated by environmental context and resources, such as remuneration. Finally, decision/policy makers identified improving health system outcomes as key enablers, but emphasized the importance of program reach and cost-effectiveness. For successful implementation within our context, IMAP-Gout needs to be adapted from a pharmacist-led model to a nurse-led model.

items.title: Risk of Major Cardiovascular Events in Patients with Psoriasis, Psoriatic Arthritis, and/or Other Forms of Spondyloarthritis: A Cohort of 72,291 Biologic New Users.
items.abstract: The impact of biologic therapies (biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs [bDMARD]) used in psoriasis (Pso), psoriatic arthritis (PsA), and other forms of spondyloarthritis (SpA) on the risk of major cardiovascular events (MACE) remains controversial. We aimed to assess the risk of MACE after initiation of a bDMARD among patients with Pso, PsA, or SpA, in a real-world clinical setting. We conducted a nationwide cohort study using the French National Health Data System (SNDS). Adults with Pso, PsA, or SpA who initiated a bDMARD (tumor necrosis factor inhibitors [TNFi]; interleukin [IL] inhibitors: IL-12/23i, IL-23i, IL-17i) between 1 July, 2016, and 31 July, 2023 were eligible for inclusion. The primary outcome was incident MACE, defined as cardiovascular death and/or hospitalization for acute myocardial infarction or ischemic stroke. Inverse probability-weighted Cox models were used to estimate weighted hazard ratios and their confidence intervals. Models were further adjusted for time-varying concomitant treatments, treatment indication, year of initiation, and prior non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug use. An interaction term between bDMARD exposure and history of cardiovascular disease was included. A total of 72,291 patients were included (mean age 46.1 ± 14.2 years, 49.4% female): 10,703 IL-17i (14.8%), 7952 IL-23i (11.0%), 5962 IL-12/23i (8.2%), and 47,674TNFi (66.0%). Compared with initiators of other bDMARDs, TNFi initiators were younger and had fewer comorbidities and cardiovascular risk factors at baseline. During follow-up, 438 patients (0.6%) experienced a MACE, including 107 (0.1%) cardiovascular deaths. The median time to event was 13.5 months (interquartile range, 5.1-30.4). In crude analyses, initiation of IL-17i, IL-23i, and IL-12/23i was associated with a higher risk of MACE compared withTNFi drugs. However, among patients without a history of cardiovascular disease, after inverse probability of treatment weighting and adjustment, no significant association was observed (weighted hazard ratio [95% confidence interval]: 0.90 [0.57-1.43] for IL-12/23i, 1.12 [0.66-1.88] for IL-23i, and 1.07 [0.74-1.55] for IL-17i). Findings held across most sensitivity analyses, except for the short-term analysis restricted to the first 6 months after treatment initiation, in which a trend toward a higher MACE risk with IL-17i was observed. A trend toward a higher MACE risk with IL-17i was also observed among men, patients aged ≥ 50 years, and those with a history of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug use. However, the number of events was low, and the results did not reach statistical significance. No significant increase in MACE risk was observed with IL-12/23i, IL-23i, or IL-17i compared with tumor necrosis factor inhibitors. However, the study lacked sufficient power to draw definitive conclusions regarding a possible increased risk associated with IL-17i in patients with a high baseline cardiovascular risk profile, or the potentiation of this risk by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug use.

items.title: The smoking gun: a fortuitous case linking an ACPA surge to spontaneous vertebral fracture in quiescent rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Anti-citrullinated protein antibodies (ACPA) have been implicated in bone loss through their effects on osteoclast activity, independently of systemic inflammation. However, the relationship between changes in ACPA levels and acute fractures remains poorly understood. A woman with longstanding rheumatoid arthritis in sustained clinical remission developed a spontaneous L3 vertebral fracture without preceding trauma or evidence of active inflammation. The fracture coincided with a marked increase in ACPA levels, which had remained stable for several years. Magnetic resonance imaging confirmed an acute vertebral fracture with bone marrow edema. The patient had been receiving alendronate for 5 years because of osteoporosis. The temporal association between the fracture and the increase in ACPA levels raises the possibility of a bidirectional relationship. Longstanding ACPA positivity may contribute to bone fragility, while bone injury and the subsequent exposure of citrullinated antigens might stimulate further antibody production. This case suggests a possible association between changes in ACPA levels and vertebral fracture in rheumatoid arthritis, even in the absence of clinically active disease. However, other established risk factors for fracture were present, and causality cannot be established from a single observation. This observation is hypothesis-generating and warrants further investigation into the potential relationship between ACPA fluctuations and skeletal fragility in rheumatoid arthritis.

items.title: Dietary patterns and odds of prevalent gout comorbidity in diabetes mellitus: a mediation analysis of glucose metabolism and renal function.
items.abstract: While independent associations between dietary patterns and diabetes mellitus (DM) or gout have been established, their relationship in comorbid conditions remains unclear. We aimed to examine the associations between distinct dietary patterns and prevalent gout among individuals with DM. We retrieved data in this cross-sectional study from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. We used logistic regression models and Restricted cubic splines to explore associations between five dietary patterns (healthy eating index 2020 (HEI-2020), dietary approaches to stop hypertension (DASH), alternate Mediterranean diet score (aMED), dietary inflammatory index, and alternative healthy diet index). We also conducted subgroup and mediation analyses. In multivariable-adjusted models, HEI-2020 (odds ratio (OR) = 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.70-0.96, P = 0.015), DASH (OR = 0.83; 95% CI = 0.70-0.98, P = 0.031), and aMED (OR = 0.86; 95% CI = 0.74-0.99, P = 0.041) scores were significantly associated with lower odds of prevalent gout among individuals with DM, with no nonlinear trends observed. Subgroup analyses revealed no significant interactions. Mediation analyses suggested that the triglyceride-glucose index-ratio of waist circumference to height mediated 40.2% and 22.8% of the effects of the DASH and HEI-2020 patterns, respectively. Serum uric acid showed evidence of mediation for the aMED pattern accounting for 16.3% of the association. Among people with DM in the USA, adherence to HEI-2020, DASH, and aMED dietary patterns is associated with lower odds of prevalent gout comorbidity in people with DM. Dietary structure improvement may therefore be associated with a lower burden of gout comorbidity in this population.

items.title: Serological and clinical outcomes of rituximab in antiphospholipid syndrome with or without SLE: a retrospective single-centre cohort.
items.abstract: To assess the dynamics of aPL titres after rituximab treatment, durability of serological responses, recurrent thrombosis, and safety in patients with APS. This retrospective study included 54 patients, predominantly with SLE-associated APS (n = 43), who received at least one course of rituximab. aCL and anti-β2-glycoprotein I (aβ2GPI) IgG/IgM were evaluated at baseline and 6-12 months after treatment. Long-term serological, clinical and safety outcomes were analysed over a median follow-up period of 4.7 years. At 6-12 months, positivity rates decreased significantly for aCL IgG (59.3% to 24.1%), aCL IgM (24.1% to 5.6%), aβ2GPI IgG (42.6% to 16.7%), and aβ2GPI IgM (20.4% to 5.6%) (all P <0.05). Long-term serological data were available for 31 patients. At last follow-up, aβ2GPI IgG positivity remained lower than baseline (P = 0.039), whereas quantitative titres were no longer significantly different. Long-term serological changes did not differ according to rituximab cycle number. Thrombotic recurrence occurred in five patients, four of whom were either off anticoagulation or had subtherapeutic INR values. Fifteen patients developed bacterial infections, seven SARS-CoV-2 infections, and five patients died during follow-up, including one who died from sepsis. Rituximab was associated with marked short-term reductions in aPL titres and positivity, although quantitative suppression was not sustained long term. Changes in aCL/aβ2GPI did not consistently reflect thrombotic risk. These findings suggest that rituximab may be a valuable adjunctive therapy in selected patients with difficult-to-treat APS, although causality cannot be established from this retrospective study.

items.title: Exploring esophageal vasculopathy in systemic sclerosis through left gastric artery Doppler ultrasound: a pilot study.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is characterized by immune dysregulation, fibrosis, and vasculopathy of the skin and internal organs. Vasculopathy is considered the fundamental pathogenetic determinant, and the gastrointestinal (GI) tract-particularly the esophagus-is among the most frequently involved organs even if its involvement is likely underestimated due to the lack of adequate screening tools. The left gastric artery (LGA) is a small vessel supplying the lower esophageal sphincter. This study aimed to assess the feasibility of Doppler ultrasound (DUS) evaluation of the LGA, and to explore whether LGA hemodynamic parameters may represent a surrogate marker of upper GI vasculopathy in SSc. A total of 38 SSc patients (ACR/EULAR 2013 classification criteria) and 25 healthy controls were enrolled. Subjects underwent DUS of the LGA performed by a single expert operator. The size and arterial blood flow of the LGA were evaluated, and Doppler parameters were measured and calculated. In 49/63 subjects (78%), among which 29 patients and 20 healthy controls, LGA was clearly visualized. Among the Doppler parameters, only RI differed significantly between groups, being higher in SSc patients (0.81 ± 0.04 vs 0.77 ± 0.08; mean difference 0.04; p = 0.041; 95% CI 0.001-0.08; Cohen's d = 0.620). LGA can be visualized using DUS in a substantial proportion of subjects. The observed increase in RI in SSc patients is a preliminary finding that may reflect underlying vasculopathy, and is in line with the vascular involvement which characterizes the disease, although its clinical significance remains to be established. Given the small sample size, the exploratory nature of this finding and potential confounders, larger studies are needed to confirm these preliminary results and to determine whether age- and sex-specific cutoff values may be clinically meaningful. Key Points • Doppler ultrasound allows feasible assessment of the left gastric artery in the majority of patients with systemic sclerosis. • Systemic sclerosis patients showed higher left gastric artery resistive index values, suggesting a possible association with upper gastrointestinal vasculopathy. • These preliminary findings support left gastric artery Doppler ultrasound as a technique worth further study in systemic sclerosis, warranting larger validation cohorts to confirm their clinical relevance.

items.title: Probable Acromioclavicular Joint Gout in Two Patients With Longstanding Gout: A Report of Two Cases.
items.abstract: Acromioclavicular (AC) joint gout is uncommon and can be difficult to distinguish from infection or degenerative disease without synovial crystal confirmation. We describe two older men with longstanding, intermittently treated gout who presented with symptomatic AC-joint abnormalities. A 74-year-old man had four months of bilateral AC-joint swelling, peripheral tophi, hyperuricemia, erosive radiographic changes, and supportive ultrasonographic findings, including a double-contour sign at the knee. A 94-year-old man had three months of right AC-joint pain and swelling, hyperuricemia, radiographic irregularity, and ultrasonographic synovial changes with power Doppler activity. Neither patient had an accessible AC-joint effusion for aspiration; therefore, crystal identification and bacterial culture were unavailable. The findings were compatible with probable AC-joint gout, but infection could not be definitively excluded, especially in the second patient, whose C-reactive protein was 74 mg/L. Colchicine and long-term urate-lowering therapy were prescribed; treatment details and standardized longitudinal outcomes were incompletely documented. These cases emphasize cautious diagnostic interpretation of unusual-site gout without tissue confirmation.

items.title: Association between serum uric acid level and bone mineral density in Chinese gout patients: a cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Previous studies have suggested that elevated levels of serum uric acid (sUA) exert significant protective effects against osteoporosis in healthy individuals. However, the effects of sUA levels on bone mineral density (BMD) and bone turnover markers (BTMs) in gout patients, as well as the risk factors for osteopenia in this population, remain unclear. Our study aimed to analyse the risk factors for osteopenia in gout patients and investigate the effects of sUA levels on bone metabolism. Patients were categorized into two groups based on their BMD, including the low BMD group (comprising both osteopenia and osteoporosis patients, given the small number of individuals in the osteoporosis subgroup) and the normal BMD group. We compared their clinical characteristics, incorporated sUA into a logistic regression analysis and applied restricted cubic splines (RCSs) to evaluate potential nonlinear dose-response relationships. Multivariate linear regression models were subsequently used to investigate the associations between sUA levels and BMD. Furthermore, subgroup analyses were performed. Compared with patients in the normal BMD group, patients in the low BMD group were older and had significantly greater sUA levels but lower BMI values ( P  < 0.05). Logistic regression analysis revealed that high sUA levels were an independent risk factor for osteopenia. RCS analyses revealed a linear relationship between sUA levels and the risk of osteopenia. Multivariate linear regression analyses adjusted for sex, age, body mass index (BMI), and other potential confounders demonstrated a significant negative correlation between sUA levels and BMD at all skeletal sites. Furthermore, subgroup analyses revealed an inverse association between sUA levels and lumbar spine BMD in participants with a BMI <28 kg/m 2 and those aged ≥ 50 years. Among hospitalized patients with stable-stage gout, sUA levels were negatively associated with BMD in gout patients . Higher sUA levels (particularly > 9.4 mg/dL) were linked to a greater likelihood of low BMD, especially in older and nonobese individuals.

items.title: Microenvironment-Triggered Sequentially Targeted Micelles for Dual Regulation of Macrophages and Fibroblast-Like Synoviocytes via ROS-Responsive Rg1 Release and HAP-1-Mediated Celastrol Delivery in Rheumatoid Arthritis Therapy.
items.abstract: Excessive proliferation of invasive fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS) and persistent synovial inflammation inevitably drive the pathological progression of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). A drug delivery system enabling dual regulation of macrophages and FLS is highly desirable for RA treatment. We fabricated microenvironment-triggered sequentially targeted micelles (HAP@CMR) co-loaded with ginsenoside Rg1 (Rg1) and celastrol (Cel) for dual regulation of macrophages and FLS. Rg1 was conjugated to the micelle surface via a ROS-responsive linker. Within the ROS-overexpressing joint microenvironment, ROS-triggered cleavage of the Rg1 shell unmasked the HAP-1 targeting peptide to facilitate FLS endocytosis alongside selective Rg1 release, which suppressed macrophage-mediated inflammation. Cel was selectively internalized by FLS through the exposed HAP-1 peptide to inhibit FLS proliferation. In vitro, HAP@CMR repolarized macrophages from the pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, suppressed inflammatory cytokine secretion, and exerted potent inhibitory effects on the proliferation, migration, and invasion of FLS. In a rat collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) model, administration of HAP@CMR led to the most pronounced reduction in paw swelling among all drug-treated groups. Further histological, X-ray, and micro-CT assessments confirmed that this treatment effectively alleviated synovial inflammation, attenuated cartilage erosion, and inhibited bone destruction. This novel nanoplatform promotes FLS apoptosis while mitigating local inflammatory responses, providing a promising therapeutic strategy for RA.

items.title: Association of Plasma CCDC88A Expression Combined with Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate with Rheumatoid Arthritis Disease Activity: A Cross-Sectional Exploratory Study.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) disease activity is assessed using composite clinical indices that combine examination findings, patient and physician‒reported assessments, and laboratory markers. Circulating RNA may provide complementary molecular information, but evidence for plasma RNA markers of current RA activity remains limited. To identify plasma RNA transcripts associated with cross-sectional RA disease activity and to explore whether plasma RNAs concentration provides complementary discriminatory information when combined with hematological parameters. This cross-sectional, two-stage study used targeted RNA sequencing to screen plasma from 25 patients with established RA and 14 healthy controls (HCs). Patients with RA were categorized as having high disease activity (HDA; DAS28-ESR >5.1, n=13) or low disease activity/remission (LDA/remission; DAS28-ESR ≤3.2, n=12). The expression of the leading candidate, CCDC88A , was assessed by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) in 108 plasma samples, including 78 patients with RA and 30 HCs. Plasma CCDC88A expression was lower in patients with RA than in HCs (median [interquartile range], 0.55 [0.29-0.81] vs 0.94 [0.59-1.12]; p=0.003). For cross-sectional discrimination between moderate activity and LDA/remission, the area under the curve (AUC) was 0.659 for CCDC88A , 0.746 for erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), and 0.785 for their combination. Molecular markers, when combined with peripheral blood-derived parameters, such as ESR, may potentially serve as supporting indicators of RA disease activity.

items.title: Research progress of mitophagy and its targeted therapeutic strategies in rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic, systemic autoimmune inflammatory disease characterized by persistent joint inflammation and progressive bone destruction. In recent years, mitophagy-a selective form of autophagy-has garnered increasing attention. As a critical cellular process, mitophagy specifically removes damaged mitochondria and maintains mitochondrial homeostasis and energy metabolic balance. Accumulating evidence suggests that mitophagy not only regulates cell survival and metabolic reprogramming but also plays a central role in preserving immune homeostasis, modulating immune cell polarization, and suppressing inflammatory signaling. This article reviews the molecular mechanisms of mitophagy and its pivotal role in RA, along with recent advances in mitophagy-targeted therapeutic strategies, aiming to provide novel insights for RA treatment.

items.title: In vivo monitoring of polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells in experimental rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) regulate immune responses, but their role in autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA) remains incompletely understood. Here, we applied non-invasive positron emission tomography (PET) imaging to investigate the migration dynamics of polymorphonuclear (PMN)-MDSCs in experimental RA. RA was induced in female BALB/c mice via K/BxN serum. Immune infiltrates in arthritic ankles were characterized by flow cytometry and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)-based proteomics. We radiolabeled bone marrow-derived (BM-PMN-MDSCs) and RA ankle-derived PMN-MDSCs (RA-PMN-MDSCs) intracellularly with [ 64 Cu]Cu-PTSM or Ly6G-specific [ 64 Cu]Cu-NOTA-1A8. Radiolabeled PMN-MDSCs were adoptively transferred into RA mice and tracked longitudinally by PET/MRI. In a second cohort, [ 64 Cu]Cu-NOTA-1A8 was injected directly for in vivo imaging of Ly6G + myeloid cells over 48 h. RA progression was associated with a marked increase in the number of CD11b + Ly6C med Ly6G + PMN-MDSCs in arthritic ankles, whereas the number of CD11b + Ly6C high Ly6G - monocytic-MDSCs remained unchanged. PET/MRI demonstrated significantly enhanced homing of RA-PMN-MDSCs to inflamed ankles compared with that of BM-PMN-MDSCs, indicating disease-associated functional adaptation. Direct in vivo targeting of MDSCs with [ 64 Cu]Cu-1A8 revealed strongly increased uptake in arthritic ankles at 1 h, 24 h, and 48 h p.i. , which was significantly reduced by Ly6G blockade, confirming tracer specificity. Proteomic analysis revealed enrichment of extracellular matrix organization and integrin signaling pathways in RA-PMN-MDSCs, suggesting that a distinct inflammatory signature underlies their migratory behavior. PET/MRI enables non-invasive monitoring of PMN-MDSC migration during experimental RA and provides novel insights into the role of these cells in autoimmune inflammation, supporting the development of PMN-MDSCs as biomarkers and therapeutic targets in autoimmune diseases.

items.title: Persistent Bacillus cereus bacteremia in a patient with systemic sclerosis-associated intestinal pseudo-obstruction: A case report.
items.abstract: Bacillus cereus is a spore-forming, Gram-positive rod often considered a blood culture contaminant but can cause persistent bacteremia, particularly in patients with intravascular catheters or impaired mucosal barriers. Optimal management without an identifiable source remains unclear. We describe a 62-year-old woman with diffuse systemic sclerosis (CREST spectrum, not on immunosuppressive therapy) complicated by interstitial lung disease, pulmonary arterial hypertension, and chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction requiring total parenteral nutrition via a tunneled central venous catheter. She presented with rhabdomyolysis and dehydration and was found to have persistent Bacillus cereus bacteremia. Blood cultures remained positive for nearly two weeks despite catheter removal and susceptibility-guided antimicrobial therapy. Extensive evaluation, including transthoracic echocardiography, cardiac CT, PET-CT, and an indium-111-labeled white blood cell scan, revealed no endocarditis or any other source. Bacteremia cleared only after gentamicin was added to vancomycin. Despite recommendations to continue intravenous therapy, she completed treatment with oral clindamycin because of financial and personal constraints. Bacteremia persisted for nearly two weeks despite catheter removal, arguing against a purely device-related source and suggesting occult gastrointestinal translocation driven by the mechanical and mucosal consequences of severe systemic sclerosis-associated gut dysmotility rather than pharmacologic immunosuppression. Clearance required combination antimicrobial therapy, highlighting the gut as a potential occult reservoir for bacteremia in patients with severe intestinal pseudo-obstruction, and suggesting that diffuse, nonspecific findings on functional imaging may serve as a diagnostic clue when no discrete source is identified.

items.title: Assessment of damp-heat impeding syndrome in rheumatoid arthritis: development and validation of a diagnostic scale.
items.abstract: To develop a novel quantitative scale for Damp-Heat Impeding Syndrome (DHIS) in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and to enhance diagnostic reliability through a combined consensus- and data-driven approach grounded in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) principles, thereby addressing the limitations of existing expert-consensus-based tools. Scale items were selected from the China Rheumatoid Arthritis Registry of Patients with Chinese Medicine (CERTAIN) database, a prospective, multicenter, observational disease registry for RA patients receiving TCM treatment, and refined through expert consultation. Based on TCM theory and clinical guidance, items were categorized into three domains: disease-related, heat-related, and dampness-related. A two-stage statistical method was applied to estimate item scores and determine cutoff values for each domain. According to TCM diagnostic principles, DHIS is identified only when the scores in all three domains exceed their respective thresholds. To enhance clinical applicability, two versions of the scale were developed: one including pulse manifestations and one excluding them. The dataset was divided based on follow-up time into a development set ( n = 6680) and a validation set ( n = 3882), both from the CERTAIN database. A DHIS diagnostic scale was developed with two versions: Version 1 included pulse manifestations (11 items), and Version 2 excluded them (10 items). The scale comprised three domains: disease-related, heat-related, and dampness-related. Key symptoms included joint pain as well as tongue and pulse features such as yellow tongue coating and slippery pulse. Secondary symptoms included sticky stool and greasy tongue coating. In the development set, Version 1 achieved a Youden index of 0.83 and sensitivity of 0.89; in the validation set, it achieved 0.78 and 0.86, respectively. Cronbach's α was 0.78 for Version 1 and 0.75 for Version 2. Both versions of the DHIS diagnostic scale demonstrated good internal consistency and strong diagnostic performance, supporting their utility in identifying DHIS among RA patient.

items.title: Analysis of Factors Associated With Interstitial Lung Disease in Treatment-Naïve Rheumatoid Arthritis Patients and Development of a Classification Nomogram.
items.abstract: Interstitial lung disease (ILD) is a serious extra-articular manifestation of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and contributes substantially to morbidity and mortality. Early identification of RA-associated ILD (RA-ILD) remains challenging, and reliable biomarkers for risk stratification are lacking. This study aimed to identify cytokine-related factors associated with RA-ILD and to develop an exploratory classification model for assessing the presence of ILD in patients with newly diagnosed, treatment-naïve RA. A total of 66 newly diagnosed, treatment-naïve RA patients were enrolled, including individuals with and without ILD confirmed by high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT). All patients were disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (DMARD)-naïve and had not received glucocorticoids or biologics prior to enrollment. Plasma IL-22 concentration was measured by ELISA; other cytokines (IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-17A, IFN-γ, and TNF-α) were quantified using a multiplex bead-based immunoassay. Clinical characteristics, laboratory parameters, and radiological findings were collected. Feature selection was performed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and Boruta algorithms, followed by multivariable logistic regression to identify independent factors associated with RA-ILD. A nomogram was constructed based on selected predictors, and its performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis and cross-validation. Patients with RA-ILD exhibited distinct cytokine profiles compared with those without ILD. Multivariable analysis identified age, smoking, lower mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC), higher plasma TNF-α levels and lower plasma IL-22 levels as independent factors associated with RA-ILD. The nomogram exhibited good discriminative performance, with a fivefold cross-validated AUC of 0.851 (95% CI: 0.755-0.947); the apparent AUC in the full sample was 0.87. Internal validation indicated acceptable model stability. Age, smoking, MCHC, higher plasma TNF-α levels and lower plasma IL-22 levels were associated with the presence of ILD in newly diagnosed, treatment-naïve RA patients. The proposed cytokine-based nomogram may serve as a hypothesis-generating tool for early identification of RA-ILD. Further validation in larger, independent cohorts is warranted before clinical application.

items.title: Correlations between serum acute-phase protein SAA, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, and disease activity in ankylosing spondylitis.
items.abstract: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a chronic inflammatory rheumatic disease characterized by sacroiliitis and spinal osteophyte formation that needs sophisticated testing to improve the accuracy of activity assessment and clinical decision-making. To investigate the clinical value of serum amyloid A (SAA) and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) in assessing disease activity in patients with AS. Using the bath ankylosing spondylitis disease activity index (BASDAI), 160 AS patients were categorized into 3 subgroups: low activity (BASDAI <4, n = 60), moderate activity (4≤ BASDAI <6, n = 50), and high activity (BASDAI ≥6, n = 50). Quantitative measurements included SAA concentrations and PLR values, with subsequent analysis of their relationship to disease progression. Diagnostic performance was evaluated with receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve methodology. The high-activity group showed significantly elevated SAA (48.3 mg/L ± 9.1 mg/L) and PLR (164.5 ± 29.2) versus moderate- (SAA: 29.0 mg/L ± 8.2 mg/L; PLR: 138.4 ± 27.6) and low-activity groups (SAA: 14.3 [11.7-17.2] mg/L; PLR: 102.7 ± 22.2) (all P < 0.001). Both markers correlated strongly with BASDAI (SAA: r = 0.76; PLR: r = 0.71, P < 0.001). ROC analysis demonstrated that an SAA cutoff of 30.6 mg/L predicted high activity (96% sensitivity, 80% specificity), while PLR ≥143.7 showed 78.0% sensitivity and 76.4% specificity. Combined detection achieved superior area under the curve (0.95) versus individual markers (SAA: 0.93; PLR: 0.86). SAA and PLR are strongly associated with BASDAI-defined disease activity in AS, and combined assessment improves identification of high disease activity, supporting their potential role as objective adjunctive markers in clinical assessment.

items.title: Integrative proteomic and machine learning strategies identify key biomarkers associated with response to JAK inhibitor in rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) have revolutionized the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), yet therapeutic responses vary widely across patients. Identifying proteomic biomarkers of response may enhance personalized treatment strategies and improve clinical outcomes. We conducted a prospective study involving 42 RA patients treated with tofacitinib, baricitinib, or upadacitinib. Longitudinal serum proteomic profiling was performed at baseline and 6 months using the Olink® Explore 384 platform. Treatment response was defined by ACR/EULAR criteria. Biomarkers associated with good responders were identified through differential expression analysis and ensemble feature selection. Prediction models were developed using selected features, and feature importance was quantified using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Pretreatment levels of IL-12B, IL-17A, and IFN-γ were significantly elevated in JAKi non-responders. IL-17 signaling was associated with response to baricitinib and tofacitinib, while upadacitinib responders exhibited broader suppression of immune-related proteins including IL-4/IL-13 pathways. Prediction models using proteomic features outperformed those based on clinical variables alone (AUC ≥ 0.90 vs. 0.52 - 0.57), with further improvement upon integrating clinical and proteomic data (AUC = 0.95). Among all features, IL-12B emerged as the most robust and consistent predictor of treatment response, supported by both differential expression and multiple machine learning approaches. Serum proteomic profiling identifies elevated pretreatment IL-12B levels as a key predictor of JAKi non-response and uncovers distinct molecular responses to different JAK inhibitors. These findings support the utility of integrating proteomics with machine learning to advance personalized treatment strategies in RA.

items.title: Characteristic central nervous system fingerprints and related molecular signatures in difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Despite guideline-recommended treatment, approximately 30% of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients remain symptomatic and are classified as difficult-to-treat (D2T), representing an unmet clinical need. D2T RA is a heterogeneous state potentially involving differences across several biological and psychological levels, but the exact underlying mechanisms remain unclear. To capture this complexity, our multimodal cross-sectional study aimed to characterize the contributing factors of the D2T state with a multimodal approach. 31 D2T RA (defined by EULAR, 2021), 18 non-D2T RA patients, and 32 healthy controls (HCs) were included. All participants underwent a clinical assessment, psychological analysis (in-depth interviews, the Rorschach test, and questionnaires), two resting-state functional MRI (fMRI) scans with standardized heat pain stimulation in between, and peripheral blood transcriptomic analysis. The activity and connectivity of brain regions, especially the somatosensory cortex and the posterior cingulate cortex, one of the main hubs of the default mode network (DMN), showed significant alterations in D2T RA. Furthermore, acute pain stimulation influenced connectivity patterns of D2T patients differently compared to non-D2T patients and HCs. These results are in line with the psychological profiles of D2T patients characterized by cognitive, coping, and emotional dysregulations as well as altered pain processing. Transcriptomic analysis identified mediators, pathways, and signaling mechanisms such as neuregulin 1 (NRG1) and type I interferon signaling associated with neuroinflammation and synaptic plasticity. Our findings identify central nervous system (CNS) alterations as a meaningful contributor to the D2T RA phenotype, helping to explain persistent symptom burden beyond inflammation. These characteristic neuroimmune signatures support multidisciplinary, personalized interventions that target CNS processes alongside inflammation control to improve outcomes.

items.title: Isolated renal involvement in IgG4related disease presenting with dual ANCA positivity.
items.abstract: IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is a rare fibroinflammatory disorder that can affect almost any organ and is characterized by a lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate, obliterative phlebitis, and storiform fibrosis. It is often associated with eosinophilia and elevated serum IgG4 levels. Isolated renal involvement is relatively uncommon. Several other conditions may mimic IgG4-RD clinically and radiologically, for example antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis, lupus nephritis, lymphoma, inflammatory pseudotumor, drug-induced tubulointerstitial nephritis (TIN), Sjogren syndrome-associated tubulointerstitial nephritis, and sarcoidosis. We present a case of 55-year male who presented with complaints of bilateral lower limb swelling and frothing of urine. Laboratory investigations revealed elevated serum creatinine, subnephrotic proteinuria, and bland sediments. ANCA were elevated. Renal biopsy showed lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, with storiform fibrosis and raised IgG4-positive plasma cells, fulfilling the criteria for IgG4-related tubulointerstitial nephritis. Later serum IgG and IgG4 levels also came out also elevated. However, the presence of ANCA was a confounding factor in the present case. The patient was initiated on steroid therapy. Patients with biopsy-proven IgG4-RD may have positive ANCA with specificity for myeloperoxidase or proteinase-3, with or without an overt ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV). Thus, the presence of concurrent ANCA autoantibodies has no clinical implication unless accompanied by clinical and histological features of AAV.

items.title: High-Titer Antinuclear Antibody Defines a Distinct IgG4-Related Disease Subset With Predilection for Lung and Kidney Involvement.
items.abstract: This study investigated whether antinuclear antibody (ANA) positivity identifies a distinct clinical phenotype in IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD), characterized by specific organ involvement patterns. We conducted a cohort study of patients diagnosed with IgG4-RD (2016-2024). Based on indirect immunofluorescence (IIF) results, patients were categorized as ANA-negative (titer ≤ 1:100) or ANA-positive, with the latter further stratified by titer: group 1 (moderate titer, 1:320) and group 2 (high titer, ≥1:1000). We comprehensively compared demographics, organ involvement, and laboratory profiles across groups. Multivariable logistic regression was used to quantify associations. Among 278 patients, 38 (13.7%) were ANA-positive (n = 19 per titer-based subgroup). ANA patterns differed: granular in group 1 versus homogeneous/granular homogeneous in group 2. Only patients in group 2 (high-titer ANA) demonstrated a significantly elevated risk of lung and kidney initial onset and involvement compared to ANA-negative patients. This group also exhibited marked hypocomplementemia. The adjusted odds ratios for lung and kidney involvement in group 2 were 10.18 (95% CI: 3.590-28.876) and 4.42 (95% CI: 1.605-12.151), respectively. No such associations were found in group 1. IgG4-RD combined with high-titer ANA (≥1:1000), mainly presenting as homogeneous type or homogeneous granular type, characterized by a heightened propensity for lung and kidney, initial onset and involvement, and hypocomplementemia. Routine ANA testing and careful assessment of pulmonary and renal systems are warranted in these patients.

items.title: ω -3 PUFAs inhibited necroptosis of mesangial cells in a mouse model of systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: In this study, we aimed to investigate the effects of ω -3 polyunsaturated fatty acids ( ω -3 PUFAs) on necroptosis of mesangial cells in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). 16-week-old female MRL/lpr mice were used as an animal model of SLE and were randomly divided into three groups: control group, necroptosis inhibitor treatment group, and ω -3 PUFAs treatment group. The mice were administered ω -3 PUFAs or the same volume of normal saline by oral gavage every other day for 4 weeks. Mice in the necroptosis inhibitor treatment group were administered Nec-1 (a necroptosis inhibitor) via intraperitoneal injection once daily for 3 weeks. After treatment, spleens and perirenal lymph nodes were harvested and weighed. Serum anti-dsDNA levels were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, and urinary protein levels were quantified. Renal pathology was evaluated using H&E and PAS staining. Renal IgG and C3 deposition was detected by immunofluorescence staining. Necroptosis-associated proteins were determined by immunofluorescence and Western blotting. Mesangial cells were treated with TNF- α , SM164, and Z-VAD-FMK to induce necroptosis and then supplemented with ω -3 PUFAs or Nec-1, respectively. The necroptosis of mesangial cells was assessed by Western blot, immunofluorescence staining, and flow cytometry. The inflammatory cytokines of mesangial cells were measured by RT-qPCR. ω -3 polyunsaturated fatty acids significantly ameliorated SLE-like symptoms in MRL/lpr mice, including attenuating splenomegaly and lymphadenopathy, alleviating renal pathology and lymphocyte infiltration, and decreasing renal immune complex deposition. Serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, and urinary protein levels were significantly down-regulated. Furthermore, ω -3 PUFAs treatment decreased inflammatory cytokines and inhibited necroptosis of mesangial cells in the kidneys of MRL/lpr mice. In vitro experiments demonstrated that ω -3 PUFAs inhibited necroptosis and reduced the release of inflammatory cytokines in mesangial cells. The results demonstrated that ω -3 PUFAs ameliorated the symptoms and attenuated necroptosis in renal mesangial cells in SLE mice. These findings suggest that ω -3 PUFAs might represent a novel therapeutic strategy for the treatment of SLE.

items.title: CXCL13 rs355687 variant confers increased susceptibility to systemic lupus erythematosus in a Mexican population.
items.abstract: C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 13 (CXCL13) regulates B-cell trafficking, lymphoid neogenesis, and adaptive immune responses, and its dysregulation contributes to systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) pathogenesis. Nevertheless, how CXCL13 genetic variants influence SLE susceptibility remains unclear. This study investigated the association between the CXCL13 single-nucleotide variant (SNV) rs355687 and susceptibility to SLE. This study enrolled SLE patients and healthy blood donors. Genotyping of the rs355687 SNV was performed via real-time PCR, while serum CXCL13 levels were quantified by ELISA. Genotype and allele frequencies were compared between groups, and their association with SLE risk was evaluated under different genetic models. A total of 149 SLE patients and 98 healthy controls were studied. The rs355687 minor allele frequency was significantly lower in SLE patients than in controls. The TT genotype was associated with an increased risk of SLE under both additive (odds ratio [OR] = 1.77, 95% CI: 1.13-2.76; p  = 0.01) and recessive (OR 2.03, 95% CI: 1.16-3.56; p  = 0.01) models. Furthermore, median serum CXCL13 concentrations were significantly higher in patients carrying the TT genotype compared with controls (71.51 [IQR: 51.36-149.50] vs. 57.38 [IQR: 49.52-64.97] pg/mL; p  = 0.02). The CXCL13 rs355687 SNV is associated with increased susceptibility to SLE, with the TT genotype specifically linked to elevated CXCL13 levels. These findings support the potential of this variant as a biomarker for disease susceptibility in SLE.

items.title: In-vitro exposure to mercury chloride, with and without n-3 long chain polyunsaturated fatty acids, on the Th17-associated immune response in peripheral blood mononuclear cells from systemic lupus erythematosus patients.
items.abstract: T H 17 cytokines are implicated in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) pathogenesis. Mercury is an environmental factor associated with the exacerbation of SLE pathology, potentially by regulating the Th H 17 pathway. Humans are primarily exposed to mercury from dental amalgams and fish consumption. Fish are also a rich source of the n-3 long chain polyunsaturated fatty acids, eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), and have been shown to reduce SLE disease symptoms. This pilot in-vitro investigation isolated peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) from SLE patients ( N  = 15) and healthy controls (HC, N  = 15). The cells were stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and exposed to 200 nM of mercury (II) chloride (HgCl) for 24 hr, with or without pre-exposure (24 hr) to either EPA or DHA at 100 μM each. The T H 17-associated cytokines were quantified in the PBMC supernatants. Pre-exposure to EPA resulted in significantly lower concentrations of IL-27 in supernatants of LPS-HgCl treated PBMC from SLE patients (29.58 [± 22.62] pg/mL) compared to HCs (51.63 [± 42.96] pg/mL) ( p  = 0.04). While DHA-LPS-HgCl had significantly lower IL-27 concentrations compared in LPS-HgCl in PBMC from SLE patients and HCs, there was no significant difference between groups. IL-27 exhibits pro/anti-inflammatory effects on the immune system. We suggest that the observed reductions in IL-27 concentrations following EPA-LPS-HgCl treatment support the protective role of n-3 PUFA in autoimmune responses.

items.title: Genetic Prioritization of BTN3A2 Reveals an Interferon-Responsive T-Cell Program in Dermatomyositis Through Single-Cell Mendelian Randomization and Multi-Omics Integration.
items.abstract: Dermatomyositis (DM) is a complex autoimmune disorder characterized by genetic susceptibility and dysregulated immune activation. However, the relationship between genetic variation and specific immune cell states remains poorly understood. We aimed to identify genetically supported immune-cell-specific molecular programs underlying DM and investigate their biological relevance. We integrated immune-cell-specific single-cell expression quantitative trait loci (sc-eQTLs) from the OneK1K cohort with DM genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR). Candidate genes were replicated using an independent sc-eQTL dataset and prioritized by Bayesian colocalization. Multi-tissue validation was performed using skeletal muscle transcriptomics, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC), and skin single-cell RNA sequencing, protein expression data, clinical phenotypes, virtual knockout analysis, and gain-of-function analyses of BTN3A2. We identified 204 immune cell-specific eGenes associated with DM and prioritized four high-confidence genes, including HLA-DRB1, HLA-C, Lnc-HLA-B-2, and BTN3A2. BTN3A2 showed robust colocalization across multiple CD4 + and CD8 + T-cell subsets and was further supported by muscle transcriptomic data. BTN3A2 was consistently upregulated in both DM muscle tissues and PBMCs and was broadly expressed across T-cell, NK-cell, and B-cell populations. BTN3A2 + T cells exhibited enhanced cytotoxic, activation, antigen-presentation, and interferon-responsive programs, which were reproduced in circulating PBMCs and lesional skin T cells. BTN3A2 expression was negatively correlated with MMT8 scores, while in silico knockout analysis implicated interferon-stimulated and antiviral pathways. Integrating cell-type-specific genetic evidence with multi-tissue immune profiling identified BTN3A2 as a genetically supported candidate associated with DM and an interferon-responsive T-cell state, providing novel insights for future mechanistic investigation.

items.title: Sustained Tocilizumab and Adjunctive HydroBox Therapy in Refractory Takayasu Arteritis: An 11-year Case Report.
items.abstract: Takayasu arteritis (TAK) is a rare, chronic granulomatous large-vessel vasculitis predominantly affecting young women, characterized by progressive stenosis and occlusion of the aorta and its major branches. Despite advances in biologic therapy, refractory disease with recurrent vascular complications remains a significant clinical challenge. Molecular hydrogen-based adjuvant (HydroBox) therapy has emerged as a promising adjuvant approach owing to its antioxidant and immunomodulatory properties. This report aims to describe the long-term clinical course and therapeutic outcomes of a patient with refractory TAK managed with sustained tocilizumab and HydroBox-assisted immunomodulatory therapy over 11 years. We report the case of a 25-year-old female with refractory TAK first diagnosed at age 13, presenting with sudden vision loss, dizziness, and pulseless upper extremities. Disease course was complicated by extensive great-vessel involvement, multiple cerebral infarctions, and recurrent in-stent restenosis despite ongoing interleukin-6 (IL-6) blockade. Over 50 courses of tocilizumab (Actemra) were administered from 2014 onward, combined with multiple percutaneous transluminal angioplasty and stenting procedures. HydroBox-assisted immunomodulatory therapy was subsequently introduced as an adjunctive treatment. During continued follow-up, the patient remained clinically stable with sustained suppression of inflammatory markers and favorable cerebrovascular findings on serial imaging. This 11-year case report documents the feasibility of sustained long-term tocilizumab therapy combined with adjunctive HydroBox therapy in a patient with refractory TAK. Despite extensive multi-vessel involvement, recurrent in-stent restenosis, and prior cerebrovascular ischemia, the patient achieved progressive hemodynamic stabilization, durable suppression of inflammatory markers, and continued disease control. The potential immunomodulatory and antioxidant properties of HydroBox-assisted therapy warrant further prospective investigation to establish standardized protocols and confirm efficacy in larger cohorts.

items.title: In Vivo Dynamics of Immunoregulatory Lymphocyte Reconstitution: A Seven-year Longitudinal Study of Sustained Remission in Class IV Lupus Nephritis Following Rituximab Therapy.
items.abstract: Rituximab (RTX)-induced B-cell depletion is an established treatment for refractory lupus nephritis (LN). However, the in vivo kinetics of B-cell reconstitution and their association with sustained clinical remission remain poorly characterized. Because cluster of differentiation 19-positive (CD19 + ) B-cell monitoring provides a practical measure of immune reconstitution after RTX therapy, we investigated the longitudinal in vivo immunophenotypic recovery of B-cell subsets in a patient with refractory Class IV LN who achieved durable remission. A 20-year-old woman presented in 2019 edema, nephrotic proteinuria (8.1 g/day), hematuria, hypoalbuminemia, anemia, and acute kidney injury. Laboratory investigations revealed an antinuclear antibody (ANA) titer >1:1,280, anti-double-stranded DNA (anti-dsDNA) antibodies of 2,525 IU/mL, and hypocomplementemia. Renal biopsy confirmed Class IV lupus nephritis with diffuse proliferative glomerulonephritis and a full-house immunofluorescence pattern. Treatment with intravenous methylprednisolone, RTX, hydroxychloroquine, and immunosuppressive therapy resulted in complete depletion of CD19 + B cells (46.83% to 0%), accompanied by marked reductions in anti-dsDNA antibody levels and improvement in renal function. During seven years of follow-up, CD19 + B cells gradually reconstituted to approximately 20%; however, sustained clinical remission was maintained, with stable renal function, persistently low anti-dsDNA antibody levels, normalization of complement levels, no renal flare, and progressive decline of Antinuclear antibody (ANA) titers to 1:40 and became undetectable. The case demonstrates a persistent dissociation between peripheral CD19 + B-cell repopulation and renal disease activity in vivo . The findings suggest that the quality of immune reconstitution, rather than the absolute number of CD19 + B cells, may be associated with sustained remission after RTX therapy and support the potential value of longitudinal immunophenotypic monitoring.

items.title: Implementing Routine Mental Health Screening and Structured Follow-up for Youth With Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis: A Single-center Quality Improvement Project.
items.abstract: Youth with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) have higher rates of anxiety and depression, yet pediatric rheumatology clinics rarely embed systematic mental health care into routine care. Unrecognized symptoms can impair physical functioning and disease management. The objectives of this quality improvement initiative were to increase (1) anxiety/depression screening from 0% to ≥75% and (2) algorithm-concordant follow-up for youth screening positive from 0% to ≥75%. Our team implemented iterative plan-do-study-act cycles in a pediatric rheumatology clinic at McMaster Children's Hospital. A key driver diagram and fishbone analysis informed interventions, including workflow redesign, staff training, electronic medical record supports, and a standardized follow-up algorithm. We screened youth with JIA 12-18 years of age using the Patient Health Questionnaire-4 (PHQ-4), an ultra-brief self-report tool used to detect anxiety and depression. Process measures included the percentage of eligible visits with PHQ-4 screening completed and the percentage of screened visits with documented algorithm-concordant follow-up. Outcome measures captured screening results while balancing measures assessed patient and healthcare provider acceptability. PHQ-4 screening increased from 0% to sustained percentages of ≥75% across 266 audited visits (May 2024-August 2025). Overall, 17% of youth screened positive (PHQ-4 ≥ 3). After implementing the follow-up algorithm, ≥75% of screened visits documented education, referral, and/or safety planning. Screening was acceptable to patients and health care providers, with no reported workflow disruption. Embedding PHQ-4 screening with a structured follow-up pathway is feasible and sustainable in a pediatric rheumatology clinic, supporting timely and equitable identification of mental health needs and advancing integrated biopsychosocial care for youth with JIA.

items.title: Anomalous systemic arterial supply to the basal segment of the left lung with large vessel giant cell arteritis demonstrated by 18F-FDG PET/CT.
items.abstract: We report a rare case of anomalous systemic arterial supply to the basal segment of the left lung (ABLL) coexisting with large-vessel giant cell arteritis (LV-GCA) in a 73-year-old woman. 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) demonstrated inflammatory involvement of both the aorta and the anomalous artery. To reduce vascular and perioperative risks, immunosuppressive therapy was initiated first, resulting in improvement in clinical and radiological findings. This case highlights the importance of controlling active vasculitis before definitive surgical treatment.

items.title: Long-term evaluation of the effectiveness and safety of autologous haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation for systemic sclerosis (NISSC1-LTE): a cohort study.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis is a rare and heterogeneous chronic autoimmune disease. It has the highest mortality of the rheumatic diseases and few treatment options exist. Autologous haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation (HSCT) is an effective and established therapeutic option in selected patients with early severe systemic sclerosis. This study aimed to evaluate the long-term safety and effectiveness of autologous HSCT in patients with systemic sclerosis in real-life clinical practice. This cohort study (NISSC1-LTE) followed up patients with systemic sclerosis included in the prospective European Society for Blood and Marrow Transplantation NISSC1 study who had undergone their first autologous HSCT for severe progressive systemic sclerosis. Follow-up data were collected from 13 participating centres in France, Germany, Netherlands, Italy, Spain, Switzerland, and Brazil. Participating centres completed a yearly case report form for each patient alive after 2 years and up to 10 years after autologous HSCT. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival, defined as survival from baseline without evidence of systemic sclerosis progression. Late complications after autologous HSCT, including malignancies, secondary autoimmune diseases, infections, and major adverse cardiovascular events were also analysed. People with lived experience of systemic sclerosis were involved in the design and conduct of this study. The NISSC1 study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02516124) and is complete. All 80 patients with systemic sclerosis who had an autologous HSCT between Dec 4, 2012, and Jan 19, 2016, were included in this long-term extension study. 12 patients were lost to follow-up, including five patients with a follow-up less than 5 years. Median age at autologous HSCT was 43 years (IQR 33-51), 57 (71%) of 80 patients were female, 23 (29%) were male, and median follow-up was 9·2 years (IQR 8·9-9·6) after autologous HSCT. Progression-free survival was 81% (95% CI 71-88) at 2 years, 72% (61-81) at 5 years, and 60% (47-71) at 10 years. 18 patients died during the study; causes of death were autologous HSCT-related in five (6%) of 80 patients, disease progression in nine (11%) patients, post-autologous HSCT malignancy in two (3%) patients, and late serious infection in two (3%) patients. 34 (43%) of 80 patients maintained remission without immunosuppressive treatment over 10 years. This study provides long-term follow-up data after autologous HSCT in patients with systemic sclerosis allowing robust assessment of response rate, late complications, and sustained treatment benefit. The extended timeframe might serve as an important comparator for all upcoming, cellular treatment options. None.

items.title: Performance of the systemic lupus erythematosus disease activity score (SLE-DAS) in daily clinical practice: A prospective study of 125 patients in India.
items.abstract: BackgroundAccurate measurement of disease activity is a cornerstone in the management of patients with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), to assist in guiding therapeutic decisions. SLE-DAS (SLE Disease Activity Score) is designed to improve accuracy and sensitivity to change compared with the standard SLE Disease Activity Index (SLEDAI) score.ObjectivesWe aimed to assess the performance of SLE-DAS to identify flare and clinically meaningful improvement (CMI) in real-life SLE patients in India.MethodsProspective observational study at an Indian Rheumatology Clinic included SLE patients meeting 2012 SLICC and/or 2019 ACR/EULAR criteria, followed for 9 months. At baseline and subsequent follow-up, we recorded SLEDAI-2K, SLE-DAS, PGA, LLDAS, DORIS remission, prednisolone dose, and immunosuppressives; SELENA-SLEDAI flare index (SFI) was evaluated at follow-up. We assessed Spearman correlation, agreement, and discrepancies between SLEDAI and SLE-DAS for flare and improvement detection using an agreement matrix.ResultsA strong correlation was observed between SLEDAI-2K and SLE-DAS (rho = 0.954, 95% CI 0.934-0.968, p < 0.001). SLE-DAS identified CMI in 42.0% of visits compared to 34.8% by SLEDAI-2K. Flare detection sensitivity was higher for SLE-DAS (96%) than SLEDAI-2K (84%), with similar specificity (98.9%). The agreement of SLEDAS remission and low disease activity (LDA) with DORIS remission and LLDAS, respectively, was perfect (κ = 1, p < 0.001). Discordant analysis revealed that SLEDAI-2K underestimated severe flares and missed manifestations such as pneumonitis, AIHA, and serositis.ConclusionSLE-DAS demonstrated superior sensitivity, granularity, and remission alignment compared to SLEDAI-2K, supporting its adoption as a primary clinical index in diverse real-world lupus practices.

items.title: Low-level proteinuria at the initial diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus significantly increases the risk of developing proteinuria-predominant lupus nephritis.
items.abstract: A proportion of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) present with subclinical low-level proteinuria at initial diagnosis that does not meet the formal classification criteria for lupus nephritis (LN). This study aimed to investigate the association between low-level proteinuria at SLE onset and the risk of developing proteinuria-predominant LN. This was a retrospective cohort study using medical records of patients newly diagnosed with SLE from Fujian Medical University Union Hospital between December and March. Inclusion required urine dipstick proteinuria ≤2+; if quantified, protein excretion <500 mg/24h (by the urine protein-to-creatinine ratio [UPCR] or 24-hour proteinuria). Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were collected at the time of initial diagnosis, as well as urinalysis, urine sediment, UPCR, and 24-hour proteinuria during follow-up, where available. The association between various baseline variables and the subsequent development of proteinuria-predominant LN was analyzed using a Cox proportional hazards model. Of 330 patients screened, 297 were eligible for inclusion in the final analysis, of whom 85 patients had low-level proteinuria at the initial diagnosis. According to multivariable-adjusted models, low-level proteinuria significantly increased the risk of proteinuria-predominant LN (P < 0.001, hazard ratio[HR] = 3.355, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.6646.765), as did male sex (P = 0.001, HR = 3.178, 95% CI: 1.563-6.460). This study highlights that SLE patients with low-level proteinuria at initial diagnosis may require enhanced monitoring for LN, enabling early detection. Future studies are needed to determine the necessity of early intervention.

items.title: Transcriptomic age acceleration is associated with plasmablast-related immune remodeling in IgG4-related disease.
items.abstract: Biological aging profoundly influences immune function, yet its role in shaping immune remodeling within chronically inflamed tissues remains unclear. We investigated whether transcriptomic age identifies a plasmablast-associated immune aging pattern in IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD). To address this question, bulk RNA sequencing was performed on submandibular gland lesions from 49 patients with IgG4-RD and 3 controls. Transcriptomic age (tAge) was estimated using a transcriptome-based aging model, and age acceleration was calculated as the residual from chronological age. Associations between age acceleration, immune transcriptional modules, and clinical characteristics were evaluated using Spearman correlation analyses. Transcriptomic age correlated with chronological age (ρ = 0.473, P< 0.001), whereas age acceleration was associated with serum IgG4 concentrations (ρ = 0.446, P = 0.001). Among immune transcriptional modules, the plasmablast signature showed the strongest positive association with age acceleration (ρ = 0.312, nominal P = 0.029), although this association did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons (FDR-adjusted P = 0.304). Germinal center B-cell and activated B-cell programs showed inverse trends. The plasmablast module also correlated with serum IgG4 levels. Together, these exploratory findings suggest a coordinated pattern linking transcriptomic age acceleration, plasmablast enrichment, and enhanced IgG4 responses. Rather than establishing a mechanistic pathway, these findings identify a candidate plasmablast-associated immune aging pattern that warrants validation in independent cohorts.

items.title: Machine learning improves 10-year prediction of atherosclerotic plaque progression and cardiovascular events in systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: To evaluate the performance of generic and disease-adapted tools in predicting 10-year cardiovascular disease (CVD) events and atherosclerotic plaque progression risk in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), and develop a machine learning-based model to improve cardiovascular risk stratification. In a prospective 10-year follow-up carotid and femoral ultrasound study of patients with SLE without prior CVD events, we assessed the performance of 11 CVD risk scores (7 conventional, 4 SLE-adapted) to predict atherosclerotic plaque progression and incident CVD events. We used discrimination (sensitivity, specificity, area under the curve [AUC], Youden index), calibration (Brier Score [BS]) and classification (Matthews correlation coefficient, F1 score) metrics, and logistic regression and time-to-event analyses. A machine learning-based gradient boosting model was developed and internally validated. Among 111 patients (91% female, median age: 43.0 years) with 10-year ultrasonography follow-up, 53 (47.7%) developed new plaques, and 8 (7.2%) had incident CVD events. All scores demonstrated suboptimal performance; sensitivity: 0.00-0.44, AUC 0.58-0.79, and BS: 0.44-0.71. In multivariable analysis, QRISK3 was the only tool independently associated with CVD events and/or plaque progression (HR:1.87, p = 0.027). A machine learning-based score that integrates QRISK3 with disease-related risk factors (disease duration, cumulative glucocorticoid dose, DORIS achievement, antiphospholipid antibodies, hydroxychloroquine) and additional traditional CVD risk factors (physical activity, waist circumference), demonstrated significantly better performance compared to all evaluated scores. Conventional and SLE-adapted tools underestimate CVD events and atherosclerosis progression risk in SLE. A machine learning-based model incorporating disease-specific and traditional cardiovascular risk factors into QRISK3 improves CVD risk stratification.

items.title: Five items are sufficient to assess rheumatoid arthritis disease activity by patient reported outcome measure: a computer adaptive test simulation study.
items.abstract: Disease Activity (DA) monitoring is a standard of care in RA. Rasch measurement theory analyses of legacy RA DA patient reported outcome measures (PROMs) was used to develop a valid item pool of 12 items, covering five domains: Tenderness and swelling, Disease activity, Pain, Stiffness, and Physical functioning. The aim of this study was to determine whether it could be advantageous to administer these 12 RA DA items via a computer adaptive test (CAT). Simulations were conducted to assess whether the 12 RA items would cover all five domains adequately. Two sets of simulations were run with stopping rules equivalent to Cronbach's α values of 0.70 and 0.85, respectively. Further CAT simulations would have been run, if coverage of the five domains were inadequate, based on the statistical information and measurement range of the items. In both sets of initial simulations, stopping rules were most commonly satisfied after the administration of five items. However, these five items only covered three domains, with the Disease activity domain consistently missed. Two sets of five items were generated, with summary measures (maximum and mean standard error) equivalent to the initial simulations. In the context of the simulations undertaken here, a CAT does not provide any major advantage for the purposes of administering the 12 RA DA items of the item pool in comparison to administering one item from each of the five domains, and administering one item from each of the five domains appears to be sufficient. We therefore propose the development of a brief, simple to administer, and psychometrically evidenced PROM for the assessment of RA DA.

items.title: Human Adipose-Derived Stem Cell Transplantation Reverses Multiorgan Impairment in Mice with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic autoimmune disorder, leading to immune-mediated organ injury. In this study, we investigated the therapeutic effect of human adipose-derived stem cell (hADSC) transplantation on multiorgan damage in MRL/lpr mice. Conclusion These results indicate that hADSCs may ameliorate multiorgan damage associated with SLE. Urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR), serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, anti-double-stranded DNA (anti-dsDNA), interleukin-4 (IL-4), and interferon-γ (IFN-γ) levels were measured in MRL/lpr mice to evaluate changes in renal function and immune status. The spleen and lymph node indices were calculated. Heart, spleen, lymph node, skin and kidney tissues were stained to visualize pathological changes. Semiquantitative analysis of haematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining across multiple organs and Masson staining of kidneys were performed, followed by laser confocal tracing of stem cells. Compared with the model group, the hADSC-treated MRL/lpr group had significantly lower ACR, anti-ds-DNA, IFN-γ, IL-4 levels, spleen and lymph node indices ( p  < .01), and lymph node scores ( p  < .05). hADSC transplantation also improved renal dysfunction and immune function, significantly reducing pathological damage to tissues, including the kidney and heart ( p  < .01) and the spleen and lymph nodes ( p  < .05). Furthermore, hADSC treatment significantly alleviated renal fibrosis ( p  < .01) in MRL/lpr mice. These results indicate that hADSCs may ameliorate multiorgan damage associated with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
