items.title: Rheumatoid arthritis beyond the textbook: Asymmetric hand deformities with rare bilateral hallux manifestations.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic systemic auto-immune disease characterised by persistent synovial inflammation, progressive joint destruction and deformity. It classically presents as a symmetrical polyarthritis involving the small joints of the hands and feet, and this symmetry remains one of its hallmark clinical features. Foot involvement is equally common and contributes significantly to disability, although it is often under-recognised in routine clinical practice. However, asymmetric deformity progression and atypical foot manifestations are rarely highlighted in the literature.

items.title: Postural control and limits of stability are largely preserved despite increased fear of falling in patients with low disease activity Sjögren's disease: A cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: AimTo compare balance performance, posturographic measures, and limits of stability (LOS) between patients with Sjögren's disease (SjD) and healthy controls and examine associations with fatigue, functional disability, symptom burden, and fear of falling.MethodsThe study included 45 patients with SjD and 35 healthy controls. Balance was assessed using the Berg Balance Scale (BBS), computerized posturography, and LOS testing. Fatigue, symptom burden, fear of falling, kinesiophobia, and psychological symptoms were assessed using the Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy-Fatigue (FACIT-F), EULAR Sjögren's Syndrome Patient-Reported Index (ESSPRI), Falls Efficacy Scale-International (FES-I), Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia (TSK), and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), respectively. Posturographic parameters and LOS were analyzed using mixed-design repeated-measures ANOVA. Associations were examined using Spearman correlation analysis and multivariable linear regression.ResultsPatients with SjD had greater fatigue and fear of falling than controls (both p < 0.05), while BBS scores were statistically lower with a small absolute difference. No significant overall group effects were found for posturographic parameters or LOS, although group-related interactions occurred for balance score and directional LOS. Fear of falling was associated with poorer functional balance, greater fatigue, higher symptom burden, kinesiophobia, and depressive symptoms (all p < 0.05). Posturographic balance scores were not correlated with BBS, FACIT-F, TSK, or FES-I (all p > 0.05). ESSPRI remained independently associated with fear of falling (β = 0.347, p = 0.043).ConclusionIn patients with predominantly low systemic disease activity, posturographic performance was largely preserved despite increased fear of falling. Posturographic and clinical measures may capture complementary aspects of balance-related problems in SjD.

items.title: XuanBi Mitigates Rheumatoid Arthritis via Regulation of ECM-Receptor Interactions and IL-17 Signaling: Insights From Integrated Proteomic and Pharmacological Analyses.
items.abstract: Plant-derived polyphenols possess broad anti-inflammatory activities and may benefit chronic inflammatory diseases. XuanBi is a traditional Chinese medicine formula containing orally absorbable polyphenolic constituents and is used to treat rheumatoid arthritis (RA). This study investigated its absorbable components and potential mechanisms associated with synovial inflammatory hyperplasia. XuanBi was evaluated in collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) rats and rheumatoid arthritis synovial fibroblasts (RASFs). Constituents in the decoction and rat serum were characterized by high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole-Orbitrap mass spectrometry (HPLC-Q-Orbitrap-MS). Predicted targets were intersected with synovial differentially expressed proteins (DEPs), followed by network pharmacology, Gene Ontology (GO), Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses, and experimental validation. Twenty-six absorbable constituents were identified, including catechin, quercetin, baicalein, and wogonin, together with 14 candidate proteins associated with RA synovial pathology. Enrichment analysis implicated extracellular matrix (ECM)-receptor interaction, focal adhesion, and interleukin-17 (IL-17) signaling. Medium- and high-dose XuanBi reduced joint swelling, synovial hyperplasia, and inflammatory infiltration in CIA rats. In RASFs, XuanBi inhibited proliferation, migration, and invasion. It also downregulated fibronectin 1 (FN1) and caveolin 1 (CAV1), reduced phosphorylation of SRC, focal adhesion kinase (FAK), and FYN, decreased integrin alpha 2b (ITGA2B) + /integrin beta 1 (ITGB1) + cells, and reduced interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β), interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α), matrix metallopeptidase 3 (MMP3), and matrix metallopeptidase 9 (MMP9). Overall, XuanBi exerted anti-inflammatory and anti-synovial-hyperplasia effects in experimental RA, accompanied by changes in proteins associated with these pathways, supporting the potential involvement of these pathways and warranting further mechanistic and clinical investigation.

items.title: Unraveling novel bioactive phytoconstituents from Annona squamosa L. and their mechanisms of action for the relief from rheumatoid arthritis: an integrated network pharmacology, docking and MD simulations approach.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease marked by synovial inflammation, gradual joint deterioration, and extra-articular complications, resulting from a complex interplay of genetic predispositions, immune system dysregulations, and environmental factors. Synthetic medicines provide symptomatic relief but have significant side effects, limited long-term efficacy, and high costs, highlighting the need for safer and more effective multi-target therapies. Plant-derived compounds represent promising candidates for the development of novel multi-target therapeutic agents for immune-mediated and inflammatory disorders such as RA. Our study employed network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation to investigate the therapeutic effects of bioactive phytocompounds from Annona squamosa L. on RA. Bioactive phytocompounds were retrieved via systematic screening of curated databases and literature mining, followed by ADMET profiling and drug-likeness assessment. The putative targets of A. squamosa phytocompounds and RA-associated genes were identified via SwissTargetPrediction and GeneCards, respectively. Protein-protein interaction network (PPIN) analysis identified ten critical hub target genes, while Gene Ontology (GO) and KEGG pathway enrichment analyses demonstrated biological processes associated with RA pathogenesis and key signaling pathways. Four bioactive phytocompounds-quercetin, luteolin, isorhamnetin, and kaempferol-were predicted to inertact with 98 potential molecular targets, of which 50 corresponded to targets associated with RA. Ten hub target genes were identified: AKT1 , EGFR , SRC , MMP9 , GSK3B , PARP1 , MMP2 , IGF1R , KDR , and MET . Pathway enrichment analysis revealed the focal adhesion and Rap1 signaling pathways as significantly involved, alongside other biologically enriched pathways. The molecular docking demonstrated that quercetin showed the strongest binding affinity to AKT1 (- 9.7 kcal/mol). Furthermore, 100 ns MD simulation supported the stability and structural integrity of the quercetin-AKT1 complex over the entire simulation period. The findings of our investigation provide computational insights into the potential multi-target mechanisms of A. squamosa bioactive phytocompounds against RA, underscoring the necessity for further experimental validation and drug development. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40203-026-00781-7.

items.title: Bidirectional Mendelian randomization analysis reveals the causal relationship between rheumatoid arthritis and acute sinusitis.
items.abstract: This study explored the causal relationship between RA and acute sinusitis (AS) using a bidirectional Mendelian randomization (two-sample Mendelian randomization) analysis. We used publicly available genome-wide association study datasets to identify the single nucleotide polymorphisms associated with both RA and AS. We then applied statistical methods, including inverse variance weighting, MR-Egger regression, and weighted medians, to assess the causal effects between the 2 diseases. This study provides evidence through two-sample Mendelian randomization analysis, suggesting that RA may be an independent risk factor for AS. This highlights the role of immune modulation in the genetic overlap between The and AS, offering new perspectives for future research on immune disease mechanisms, and potential clinical prevention and treatment strategies.

items.title: Cardiovascular adverse events of tocilizumab and baricitinib in COVID-19 and rheumatoid arthritis: A real-world disproportionality and machine learning analysis.
items.abstract: Tocilizumab and baricitinib are used in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and COVID-19, where acute hyperinflammation and systemic stress may amplify cardiovascular risk. Comparative evidence on indication-specific cardiovascular signals remains scarce; we therefore assessed these signals by indication. We analyzed the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System data from January 2010 to June 2025 to compare cardiovascular adverse events (CVAEs) associated with baricitinib and tocilizumab. Primary outcomes included 6 CVAE categories: cardiac arrhythmias, central nervous system vascular disorders, embolic and thrombotic events, ischemic heart disease, noninfectious myocarditis/pericarditis, and other cardiac disorders. Disproportionality was assessed using the information component (IC) and reporting odds ratio (ROR), stratified by pre- and post-COVID-19 Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) periods and indications (COVID-19 vs RA). Machine learning models were additionally trained to characterize risk patterns for each drug, with feature contributions interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations. Among 17,750,053 reports, 5994 CVAEs were identified (baricitinib, n = 965; tocilizumab, n = 5029). Disproportionality was higher in the post-EUA than the pre-EUA period for both baricitinib (IC, 0.84 [IC025, 0.59] to 1.51 [1.39]; ROR, 1.89 [95% confidence interval, 1.62-2.21] to 3.22 [2.98-3.48]) and tocilizumab (0.22 [0.16] to 0.54 [0.47]; 1.18 [1.14-1.23] to 1.50 [1.43-1.57]). Baricitinib for COVID-19 showed the highest disproportionality (IC, 2.90 [IC025, 2.70]; ROR, 11.95 [95% confidence interval, 10.33-13.83]). Gradient boosting machine achieved the highest AUROC (baricitinib, 0.728; tocilizumab, 0.702), and SHapley Additive exPlanations highlighted COVID-19 indication for baricitinib and RA for tocilizumab. Our findings suggest indication-dependent cardiovascular signals when immunomodulators are repurposed for acute viral infections, underscoring the need for context-aware evaluation in drug repurposing.

items.title: Pan-immune-inflammation value and sleep disturbances in rheumatoid arthritis: A population-based NHANES study.
items.abstract: The present study sought to assess the individual and synergistic effects of pan-immunoinflammatory value (PIV) and trouble sleeping on rheumatoid arthritis (RA). We used data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey from 2005 to 2020. PIV was computed as: (neutrophil count × platelet count × monocyte count) /lymphocyte count. Trouble sleeping was assessed using a single self-reported question (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey item SLQ050), while RA case ascertainment relied on self-reported diagnosis by a physician. The associations between PIV and sleep-related RA susceptibility were interrogated through multivariable logistic regression models, with restricted cubic splines deployed to unmask potential nonlinear relationships. Effect modification was further evaluated via stratified analyses across demographic and clinical subgroups. The analytical cohort comprised 27,398 participants (2032 RA cases). In fully adjusted models, elevated PIV demonstrated a 14.9% increased RA risk in the highest versus lowest PIV quartile (Q4 vs Q1) (OR = 1.149, 95% CI:1.007-1.312), while trouble sleeping independently conferred 59.8% higher odds (OR = 1.598, 95% CI:1.449-1.761). Interaction analysis revealed that the association between PIV and RA was modulated by trouble sleeping. This study explores the association between elevated PIV, trouble sleeping, and RA. However, due to the cross-sectional nature of the data, causality cannot be inferred. The findings suggest a correlation between PIV and trouble sleeping with RA risk, but further longitudinal studies are required to establish causal relationships.

items.title: Frontiers and hotspots evolution of machine learning in gout from 2004-2023: A bibliometric analysis.
items.abstract: This study aimed to explore the evolution of frontiers and hotspots in machine learning for gout from 2004 to 2023. The database of publications was sourced from the Science Citation Index-Expanded within the Web of Science Core Collection. Employing CiteSpace 6.2.R5 software, a visual analysis of the core information within these publications was conducted. This retrieval spanned from 2004 to 2023 and was completed within the confines of a single day, specifically on October 20, 2023. In total, 219 articles were eventually included in the analysis. Publication activity remained limited before 2018 but increased markedly thereafter; 47 articles were published in 2023 by the search date of October 20. In terms of citation impact, Breiman L holds the most significant influence. China and the United States of America, along with their affiliated academic institutions, exert substantial academic influence in this field, surpassing other countries and institutions. "Ascorbic acid" is the keyword with the longest burst duration, and "prediction" holds the highest strength. The cited journals encompass various disciplines, including internal medicine, cardiology, analytical chemistry, and endocrinology and metabolism. The prevailing developmental pattern in the field of machine learning in gout primarily revolves around interdisciplinary integration. Machine learning has indeed become a frontier and hotspot in aiding the prediction and diagnosis of gout over the past 5 years. The acceptance of predictive diagnostic models and the determination of the most suitable algorithmic models remain the current and future research focal points in this field.

items.title: Isolated necrotizing scleritis revealing silent pulmonary granulomatosis with polyangiitis: A case report of rare diagnostic clue.
items.abstract: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA) is a rare, life-threatening vasculitis characterized by necrotizing granulomatous inflammation. Isolated necrotizing anterior scleritis as the sole initial manifestation is distinctly rare. The presence of a clinically silent pulmonary mass without ear, nose, and throat or renal involvement makes this presentation exceptional and diagnostically challenging. A 31-year-old man presented with recurrent unilateral necrotizing anterior scleritis resistant to corticosteroids and immunosuppressants, without systemic symptoms. This single-patient case report, prepared in accordance with CAse REport guidelines, revealed mildly elevated anti-proteinase 3 antibodies (25 AU/mL) in laboratory tests. Chest computed tomography unexpectedly showed a 5-cm solitary pulmonary mass. Histopathology demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells and vasculitis, confirming GPA. The patient was treated with pulsed intravenous methylprednisolone followed by monthly cyclophosphamide, then transitioned to rituximab maintenance therapy. He achieved marked improvement in ocular inflammation and visual function, with no new systemic manifestations during follow-up. This case illustrates a rare diagnostic pathway in which isolated, treatment-resistant necrotizing scleritis led to the detection of clinically silent pulmonary GPA. It highlights the importance of considering systemic vasculitis in atypical or refractory scleritis and underscores the critical role of tissue biopsy when serologic findings are mild or nonspecific. Furthermore, this first documented Middle Eastern case adds educational value for ophthalmologists and rheumatologists, illustrating that early multidisciplinary evaluation and timely rituximab therapy can prevent irreversible ocular damage and systemic progression.

items.title: Anti-GBM/ANCA double-positive crescentic nephritis in an elderly patient presenting with heart failure-like symptoms: A case report.
items.abstract: Anti-glomerular basement membrane (anti-GBM) antibody disease and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis represent the 2 leading causes of rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (RPGN). The coexistence of these conditions is rare, typically progresses rapidly, and has a poor prognosis. Elderly patients often present with nonspecific systemic symptoms, increasing the likelihood of misdiagnosis and treatment delay. A 74-year-old woman presented with a one-month history of intermittent shortness of breath, worsening progressively over ten days, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She denied hemoptysis, gross hematuria, rash, or arthralgia. Initial assessment suggested heart failure. However, laboratory results revealed severe renal impairment (creatinine: 1025.99 μmol/L). Renal biopsy demonstrated crescent formation in over 80% of glomeruli, with immunofluorescence showing linear immunoglobulin G deposits along glomerular capillary loops. Serological testing revealed markedly elevated anti-GBM antibody (>400 RU/mL) and MPO-ANCA (108.4 RU/mL) levels, together with a perinuclear ANCA (P-ANCA) pattern on indirect immunofluorescence, supporting the diagnosis of anti-GBM glomerulonephritis with concomitant MPO-ANCA positivity. Treatment included methylprednisolone pulse therapy, cyclophosphamide, and 3 plasma exchange sessions. Additional supportive measures comprised hemodialysis, antihypertensive therapy, and management of renal anemia. Although the patient's uremic symptoms improved markedly, renal function did not recover. She was discharged on hemodialysis and was subsequently transitioned to maintenance peritoneal dialysis. By January 2026, the anti-GBM antibody level had decreased markedly to 4.27 RU/mL, below the positive cutoff, and MPO-ANCA had also become negative. At the last follow-up in April 2026, the patient remained dialysis-dependent and experienced recurrent hospitalizations for pneumonia, heart failure, and acute pancreatitis. This case emphasizes that elderly patients with anti-GBM/ANCA double-positive crescentic glomerulonephritis may initially present with nonspecific symptoms, increasing the risk of incorrect diagnosis. Although combination therapy resulted in symptomatic improvement and serological remission, renal function failed to recover and dialysis dependence persisted. Screening for anti-GBM antibody and ANCA should therefore be considered in patients with unexplained rapidly progressive deterioration of kidney function or active urinary sediment, and renal biopsy should be performed promptly when clinically indicated.

items.title: Clinical and Immunological Factors Associated with Disease Activity in MPO-ANCA-Associated Vasculitis.
items.abstract: To explore clinical and immunological factors associated with disease activity in myeloperoxidase‑antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody‑associated vasculitis (MPO‑AAV), and analyze cross‑sectional correlations of renal impairment, anemia and antinuclear antibodies (ANA) with disease activity. In this retrospective study, 82 consecutive hospitalized MPO‑AAV patients (September 2023‑February 2025) were stratified into high‑ and low‑activity groups using BVAS‑3 (cut‑off >15 points). Baseline clinical and laboratory data were compared. Spearman correlation and univariate‑multivariate logistic regression were applied to evaluate correlates of high disease activity. Compared with low‑activity patients, the high‑activity group had higher serum creatinine (172.5 (86.2-310.7) vs 72.1 (52.3-103.5)), lower eGFR (46.70 ± 36.53 vs 86.92 ± 27.29) and hemoglobin (90.54 ± 20.53 vs 110.69 ± 18.43) (all P <0.001), as well as a higher rate of kidney injury (69.57% vs 13.89%, P<0.001). ANA positivity showed only marginal inter‑group difference ( P =0.075). BVAS‑3 was strongly correlated with creatinine ( r = 0.621(0.461~0.743)), eGFR ( r = -0.712(-0.801~ -0.593)), and hemoglobin ( r = -0.589(-0.716~ -0.419)) (all P <0.001). Multivariate regression identified kidney injury ( OR =17.75, 95% CI 3.63‑86.97, P <0.001) and reduced hemoglobin ( OR =0.93, 95% CI 0.89‑0.98, P =0.005) as independent correlates. ANA positivity reached significance in multivariate analysis ( OR =7.30, 95% CI 1.13‑47.37, P =0.038), but this result should be interpreted cautiously due to small sample and wide confidence intervals. In this single‑center retrospective MPO‑AAV cohort, renal injury and lower hemoglobin were independently associated with higher cross‑sectional disease activity.

items.title: Predictors of response and long-term efficacy and safety of nintedanib in systemic sclerosis-interstitial lung disease: data from an Italian multicentre study.
items.abstract: To evaluate the real-life efficacy and safety of nintedanib (NTD) in systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD) and to identify predictors of lung function progression and treatment discontinuation in a large Italian multicentre cohort. This retrospective observational study included SSc-ILD patients from 13 Italian tertiary centres who fulfilled 2013 ACR/EULAR classification criteria and initiated NTD. Clinical data were collected 12 months prior to NTD initiation, at baseline, and after 12 and 24 months. Lung progression was defined by ≥2 of the following: decline ≥5 predicted forced vital capacity (%pFVC), ≥10 predicted diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (%pDLCO), progression on HRCT, or worsening respiratory symptoms. Logistic regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of lung progression and NTD dose reduction/discontinuation. A total of 151 patients were included (69% female, mean age 60±11.9 years), 48% with diffuse and 42% with limited cutaneous SSc. Most patients (89%) received background immunosuppression, predominantly mycophenolate mofetil (MMF, 79.3%). Before nintedanib initiation, mean FVC % predicted and DLCO % predicted declined (%pFVC 75 ± 19 to 70 ± 20, p < 0.001; %pDLCO from 49 ± 18 to 45 ± 17, p < 0.001), whereas no statistically significant mean change was observed during the first 12 months after initiation (%pFVC 71 ± 18 to 72 ± 18%, p = 0.290; %pDLCO 44 ± 16 to 44 ± 15%, p = 0.646). The proportion meeting progression definition was lower after initiation than during the preceding year (65%vs 25%, p < 0.001). Concomitant MMF use was associated with lower odds of progression (OR 0.318, 95%CI 0.104-0.973). Gastrointestinal intolerance was the main cause of NTD regimen modification: 37% required dose reduction while 17% discontinued the treatment. The need for high-dose proton pump inhibitors predicted NTD dose reduction/discontinuation (OR 3.643, 95%CI 1.206-11.003). At 24 months (n = 42), lung function remained stable (%pFVC 68 ± 19 versus 69 ± 18, p = 0.725; %pDLCO 39 ± 17 versus 43 ± 19, p = 0.065) without any new safety issue. In this real-world cohort, initiation of nintedanib was followed by attenuation of pulmonary function decline through 24 months among patients with available follow-up. These findings are supportive of nintedanib effectiveness in routine care.

items.title: Astragalus Polysaccharides Alleviate Inflammatory Damage in Murine Rheumatoid Arthritis by Modulating Th17/Treg Balance via the Gut-Joint Axis.
items.abstract: Astragalus polysaccharides (APSs) have demonstrated protective effects in RA models; however, the underlying microbe-host crosstalk remains unclear. In this study, collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) was established in mice, followed by prophylactic and therapeutic APS administration. The following were then assessed: articular histopathology, splenic Th17/Treg frequencies via flow cytometry, serum and joint cytokine profiles via ELISA and immunohistochemistry, gut microbial metagenomes, and bone erosion via Safranin O-fast green staining. It was found that APS treatment significantly attenuated joint inflammation and bone destruction, rebalanced the Th17/Treg ratio, and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α and IL-17) while elevating anti-inflammatory IL-10 both systemically and locally. Subsequently, fecal microbiota from APS-treated donor mice was transplanted via oral gavage into CIA recipient mice. APS reversed RA-associated gut dysbiosis by enriching Ligilactobacillus , Lactobacillus , Limosilactobacillus , and Bacteroides , and these microbial shifts closely paralleled diminished articular inflammation and preserved bone architecture. Collectively, these findings indicate that APS mitigates RA progression by reconfiguring the gut microbial ecosystem-favoring beneficial taxa while curbing pathobionts-thereby restoring intestinal homeostasis, normalizing the Th17/Treg axis, and suppressing systemic and articular inflammatory responses.

items.title: Disease Knowledge Assessed by RAKE-T and Its Sociodemographic and Clinical Correlates in Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis Receiving Biologic and Targeted Synthetic DMARDs: A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Disease-related knowledge is important in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), particularly for patients receiving biologic (bDMARD) or targeted synthetic (tsDMARD) disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. This study aimed to assess disease knowledge using the Turkish version of the Rheumatoid Arthritis Knowledge Assessment Questionnaire (RAKE-T) in patients receiving bDMARD/tsDMARD therapy and to investigate its sociodemographic and clinical correlates. Methods: This multicenter cross-sectional study included 230 patients with RA receiving bDMARD/tsDMARD therapy at four rheumatology centers. Sociodemographic and clinical characteristics were recorded, and disease knowledge was assessed using the 45-item RAKE-T. Linear or robust regression analyses, as appropriate, were used to evaluate factors associated with total and domain-specific scores, except for the single-item comorbidity domain, which was analyzed using binary logistic regression. Results: The mean total RAKE-T score was 61.77 ± 19.00. Older age was associated with lower total RAKE-T and disease knowledge domain scores ( p = 0.033 for both). University education or higher was associated with higher total RAKE-T scores (β = 14.503, p < 0.001) and higher scores in the disease knowledge, pharmacological treatments, non-pharmacological treatments, and adaptive skills domains. Place of residence was associated with disease knowledge, self-care, and adaptive skills scores. Disease duration, duration of biologic therapy, sex, marital status, and previous biologic agent use were not significantly associated with total or domain-specific RAKE-T scores. Conclusions: Among patients with RA receiving bDMARD/tsDMARD therapy, disease knowledge was associated with age, educational level, and place of residence, whereas no statistically significant associations were observed with disease duration or duration of biologic therapy. These findings suggest that longer disease or treatment experience should not be assumed to correspond to greater disease knowledge and support periodic reassessment of educational needs and individually tailored patient education.

items.title: Kidney Involvement in Primary Sjögren Syndrome: Focus on Tubulointerstitial Nephritis.
items.abstract: Background and Objectives : Primary Sjögren's syndrome (pSS) is a systemic autoimmune disease with heterogeneous extraglandular involvement, including the kidney. Tubulointerstitial nephritis (TIN) is the hallmark kidney lesion of pSS, but its clinical and histological features, compared with other causes of TIN, remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to describe the clinical, laboratory, and histological features of biopsy-proven pSS-associated TIN (pSS-TIN) and to compare them with TIN of other etiologies. Materials and Methods : We retrospectively analyzed native-kidney biopsies (2015-2025) with histological diagnosis of TIN, from adult and pediatric patients, excluding cases with neoplasms or concomitant acute glomerular injury. Clinical, laboratory, and histological data of pSS-TIN patients were compared with other TIN etiologies using the Mann-Whitney U test, Fisher's exact test, and Spearman's correlation; p < 0.05 was significant. Results : Among 690 native-kidney biopsies, 35 showed TIN; after excluding cases with glomerular involvement, 14 patients with pSS-TIN and 16 patients with no-pSS-TIN patients were analyzed. All pSS-TIN patients were female, and biopsy occurred after a significantly longer interval from disease diagnosis than patients with no-pSS-TIN ( p = 0.018). Acute kidney injury was less frequent ( p = 0.021) and kidney function was better preserved in pSS-TIN, while the urea-to-creatinine ratio was similar between groups. Standard urinalysis was abnormal in only about half of patients in both groups. Longer disease duration correlated with lower eGFR in pSS-TIN ( p = 0.033). Predominantly chronic histological damage was associated with higher proteinuria ( p = 0.037) across the entire cohort, and germinal-center-like lymphoid structures were observed in two pSS-TIN patients with extensive acute damage. In our cohort, no statistically significant association was detected between kidney function indices and the severity of chronic damage. Conclusions : In this biopsy-based cohort, pSS-TIN showed a predominantly chronic presentation, less acute kidney injury, and a longer diagnostic interval than other TIN forms. Routine urinary and functional parameters may not reliably reflect chronic tubulointerstitial damage, highlighting the importance of careful renal screening and timely nephrological assessment, with kidney biopsy when clinically indicated.

items.title: ASAS Versus Modified New York Criteria for Ankylosing Spondylitis and Axial Spondyloarthritis: Attitudes and Utilization Among Saudi Rheumatologists.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) is classified using two principal systems, the modified New York (mNY) and the Assessment of SpondyloArthritis international Society (ASAS) classification criteria. Although developed for research, both are widely used in clinical practice. We assessed the self-reported use of, and attitudes toward, both criteria sets among rheumatologists in Saudi Arabia, including the perceived need for their modification. Methods: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted using a 23-item questionnaire adapted from a published multinational survey. Wilcoxon signed-rank, chi-square goodness-of-fit, and Fisher's exact tests were applied. Results: Among 54 respondents (estimated response rate, 22%), the ASAS criteria were rated significantly more useful (mean 4.26 vs. 3.85; Wilcoxon p = 0.001) and were used more frequently (Wilcoxon p < 0.001; high use, 75.9% vs. 57.4%) than the mNY criteria. When radiographs were negative, 90.7% reported ordering sacroiliac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Inflammatory back pain (77.8%) and dactylitis (63.0%) were most frequently rated as "very specific". Overall, 79.6% considered the ASAS criteria sufficiently specific for clinical trials, while 51.9% perceived a need to modify them. No statistically significant associations were detected between demographic variables and the outcomes examined. Conclusions: Respondents reported greater use of, and higher perceived usefulness for, the ASAS than the mNY criteria, a pattern that aligns directionally with multinational survey data. These self-reported findings may inform local education and future studies of how classification criteria and sacroiliac MRI are applied in practice.

items.title: Clinical Implications of the Age Threshold in the 2022 ACR/EULAR Classification Criteria for Takayasu Arteritis: A Real-World Study of Patients Aged over 61 Years.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives : The age item of the 2022 American College of Rheumatology (ACR) and the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) criteria for Takayasu arteritis (TAK) (the 2022 ACR/EULAR criteria) limits the reclassification of TAK among patients aged over 61 who were classified as TAK according to the 1990 ACR criteria. Therefore, we evaluated the clinical significance of the age item of the 2022 ACR/EULAR criteria. Methods : We included 22 previously TAK-diagnosed patients aged over 61 (TAK patient aged >61 years) and 41 TAK-reclassified patients aged 50-60 (controls) in this study and retrospectively reviewed their medical records. We compared the satisfied items of the 2022 ACR/EULAR criteria between the two groups and further investigated whether these 22 TAK patients aged >61 years fulfilled the criteria for other relevant diseases. Results : In terms of absolute requirements, TAK patients aged >61 years were significantly older than TAK-reclassified patients aged 50-60. However, there were no further significant differences in the additional clinical and imaging criteria between the two groups. TAK patients aged >61 years exhibited a significantly higher frequency of ascending aorta involvement than TAK-reclassified patients aged 50-60 (18.2% vs. 0%, p = 0.012). Among the 22 TAK patients aged >61 years, ten were categorized as clinically isolated aortitis, and three of the ten patients with CIA could additionally be categorized as restrictively defined-isolated aortitis. Conclusions : Our findings support the need for external validation of the current age threshold in larger cohorts from different ethnic and geographical populations.

items.title: A Pathway-Driven Computational Drug Discovery Framework Integrating Machine Learning and Virtual Screening for Identification of Anti-Rheumatoid Arthritis Natural Small Molecules.
items.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to establish a pathway-driven computational drug discovery framework integrating machine learning, target prioritization, virtual screening, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and in vitro evaluation to identify natural small molecules with potential anti-rheumatoid arthritis (RA) activity. Methods: Sixteen RA-related Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets were included, with 15 cohorts used for model development and one reserved for independent external validation. Pathway features quantified by gene set variation analysis (GSVA) were subjected to cohort-aware feature selection using a leave-one-dataset-out framework across seven machine-learning algorithms. Predictive modeling and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis were subsequently performed, followed by random-effects meta-analysis (REMA) and network analysis for candidate-target prioritization. Natural compounds were screened by molecular docking and further evaluated using ligand efficiency, multiple scoring approaches, explicit-membrane MD simulations, and a TNF-α-induced MH7A inflammatory model. Results: Ten stable RA-associated pathways were identified. The final CAT+ET model achieved ROC-AUCs of 0.783 (95% CI, 0.731-0.836) and 0.610 (95% CI, 0.496-0.720) in the internal and independent external validation sets, respectively, indicating limited cross-cohort generalizability. SHAP and cross-cohort analyses supported Complement and coagulation cascades for downstream investigation, and integrated expression and network evidence prioritized C3AR1 as a candidate target. Virtual screening identified four candidate natural compounds (SM1-SM4). Ligand-size analysis, ligand efficiency, multiple scoring approaches, and explicit-membrane MD simulations provided complementary structural and energetic assessments of these candidates. Among them, SM1 showed comparatively favorable computational characteristics and a relatively consistent reduction in the inflammatory markers IL6 and MMP3 in TNF-α-stimulated MH7A cells, accompanied by changes in C3AR1 expression. These convergent computational and experimental findings supported the prioritization of SM1 for further investigation. Conclusions: This study established a pathway-driven framework linking cross-cohort pathway identification with candidate-target prioritization and natural-product screening in RA. Complement and coagulation cascades and C3AR1 were prioritized for downstream investigation, while integrated computational and experimental evidence identified SM1 as a candidate with promising anti-inflammatory potential. Although direct compound-C3AR1 engagement and its functional involvement require further validation, the present study provides a systematic and extensible strategy for translating robust RA-associated pathway signals into candidate targets and natural compounds, offering a valuable foundation for subsequent natural-product drug discovery in RA.

items.title: Cryptococcosis After Initiation of Janus Kinase Inhibitors or Biologic DMARDs in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Three Pairwise Active-Comparator Analyses of Propensity Score-Matched TriNetX Cohorts, 2005-2025.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Comparative safety evidence for cryptococcosis during advanced rheumatoid arthritis (RA) therapy is limited. We compared newly recorded cryptococcosis after initiation of Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi), tumor necrosis factor (TNF) inhibitors (TNFi), and non-TNF biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (non-TNF bDMARDs). Methods: Three retrospective active-comparator analyses were conducted in the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network: JAKi versus TNFi, JAKi versus non-TNF bDMARDs, and TNFi versus non-TNF bDMARDs. After 1:1 propensity score matching, outcomes from day 1 to 10 years after initiation, capped at 30 June 2025, were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models. E-values assessed sensitivity to unmeasured confounding. Results: Matched cohorts included 27,833, 32,440, and 37,351 patients per group, respectively; all absolute standardized mean differences were <0.10. Events occurred in 20 JAKi and 12 TNFi initiators (hazard ratio [HR], 2.20; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.06-4.54) and in 22 JAKi and 13 non-TNF bDMARD initiators (HR, 2.15; 95% CI, 1.07-4.31). In the secondary comparison, 17 TNFi and 19 non-TNF bDMARD initiators had events (HR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.43-1.60). Point-estimate E-values for the JAKi comparisons were 3.82 and 3.72; CI-limit E-values were 1.31 and 1.34. Conclusions: JAKi initiation was associated with an approximately twofold higher hazard of newly recorded cryptococcosis than either biologic comparator, while estimated 10-year cumulative event probabilities were below 0.2% in all groups. The separately selected and matched populations do not support an indirect ranking of treatment classes. Low event counts, wide CIs, possible outcome misclassification, fixed exposure classification, and residual confounding preclude causal conclusions. The findings require independent confirmation.

items.title: Clinical Disease Activity and Power Doppler Changes Observed During a Multimodal Rehabilitation Program in Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Retrospective Longitudinal Observational Study.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Rehabilitation in active rheumatoid arthritis (RA) remains challenging, particularly regarding the dosing of physical agent modalities during inflammatory activity. We evaluated changes in clinical disease activity, inflammatory markers, and Power Doppler (PD) activity in patients with RA undergoing individualized multimodal rehabilitation. Methods: In this retrospective longitudinal study, 29 patients with RA were assessed at baseline and after 8 weeks. The program comprised 10 supervised sessions of individualized electrotherapy and therapeutic exercise over 2 weeks, followed by 6 weeks of home-based exercise. Background disease-modifying antirheumatic therapy was unchanged; 16 patients received ESR-guided methylprednisolone. Outcomes included DAS28-ESR and its components, C-reactive protein (CRP), and patient-level PD grade across a standardized joint set. Results: DAS28-ESR decreased from 6.05 ± 0.87 to 4.03 ± 0.82, with significant reductions in all its components and in CRP (all p < 0.001). Patient-level PD grade showed a significant shift toward lower grades, from a median of 2 [IQR 2-3] at baseline to 2 [IQR 1-2] at 8 weeks ( p < 0.001); 18 patients (62.1%) improved, and none worsened. Changes in DAS28-ESR and PD grade were not significantly correlated (ρ = 0.181, p = 0.348). In the 13 patients who did not receive additional glucocorticoids, DAS28-ESR decreased from 5.22 to 3.41 ( p < 0.001), while median PD grade changed from 2 [IQR 2-3] to 2 [IQR 2-2] ( p = 0.016). Conclusions: Improvements across clinical, laboratory, and ultrasound domains were observed during individualized rehabilitation delivered alongside pharmacological treatment, while the magnitude of clinical and ultrasound changes was not significantly correlated. Because of the absence of a control group, concomitant glucocorticoid and NSAID therapy, and the possibility of regression to the mean, the contribution of rehabilitation cannot be isolated from pharmacological treatment, natural disease course, and other sources of change. Controlled studies of dose-adapted rehabilitation in active RA, prescribed by the rehabilitation physician in collaboration with the rheumatologist, are warranted.

items.title: Long-Term Golimumab Treatment Persistence and Clinical Outcomes in Axial Spondyloarthritis: A Real-World Cohort from Kazakhstan.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives : Long-term real-world evidence on golimumab in axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) from Central Asia is limited. We evaluated clinical outcomes through week 144, treatment persistence through 36 months, factors associated with discontinuation, and reasons for discontinuation in Kazakhstan. Methods : This prospective observational cohort included 113 adults with axSpA enrolled at two rheumatology centers in Almaty in October 2019. All had received golimumab 50 mg subcutaneously every four weeks for at least 12 weeks before enrollment. Time zero for persistence analyses was the enrollment date. Clinical assessments were performed at baseline and weeks 12, 24, 52, 104, and 144. Treatment persistence was estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis, and factors associated with confirmed discontinuation were explored using Cox regression. Clinical responses were assessed using non-responder imputation (NRI; N = 113). Results : During 36 months, 24 patients had confirmed permanent discontinuation; two patients lost to follow-up without confirmed discontinuation were censored. Kaplan-Meier estimated persistence was 89.3% (95% CI, 83.8-95.2%) at 12 months, 79.4% (72.2-87.3%) at 24 months, and 78.5% (71.2-86.5%) at 36 months. Among 88 patients with paired baseline and week 144 assessments, the Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index (BASDAI), Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Score based on erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ASDAS-ESR), Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Functional Index (BASFI), Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Metrology Index (BASMI), and Maastricht Ankylosing Spondylitis Enthesitis Score (MASES) improved significantly (all p < 0.001). With NRI, 64.6% achieved BASDAI50, 59.3% ASDAS inactive disease, and 54.9% ASDAS major improvement at week 144. Higher Rheumatic Disease Comorbidity Index (RDCI) score (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.312, 95% CI, 1.042-1.653) and functional class III-IV versus I-II (adjusted HR 2.412, 95% CI, 1.037-5.611) were associated with higher discontinuation hazards in exploratory analyses. Loss of effectiveness was the most frequent reason for discontinuation (54.2%). Adverse events were recorded only when they led to discontinuation and therefore do not represent overall safety incidence. Conclusions : Golimumab was characterized by substantial 36-month treatment persistence and clinical improvement among patients who remained on treatment and were evaluable at week 144 ( n = 88). Full-cohort NRI analyses also demonstrated clinically relevant responses at week 144. Comorbidity burden and poorer functional class were associated with discontinuation in exploratory analyses. These findings add long-term real-world evidence from an under-represented geographic setting.

items.title: Citrullination of Collagen Type II and Epitope-Specific Antibody Responses in Rheumatoid Arthritis and Osteoarthritis: A Comparative Analysis.
items.abstract: Citrullination of various proteins including the major structural protein of articular cartilage, collagen type II (COL2), has been indicated to play a role in rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Humoral responses against citrullinated COL2 epitopes have also been examined in patients with another common arthritic disorder, osteoarthritis (OA), but have not been shown to be present in a substantial proportion of patients in the studied groups. To further investigate this issue, we assessed anti-COL2 epitope responses in patients with OA and RA, with particular focus on immune responses to the citrullinated form of one of the main COL2 epitopes associated with RA. This research was combined with experiments aiming to define the involvement of COL2 citrullination in these two prevalent arthritic disorders by evaluation of the presence of citrulline in normal hyaline cartilage and in purified joint COL2 from RA and OA patients. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISA) were performed to determine the levels of antibodies specific to COL2 epitopes (C1, U1, J1 and citrullinated C1 epitope) in blood plasma of RA patients, OA patients and control individuals that do not suffer from arthritis disorder. The relative level of citrullination of COL2 purified from normal (healthy), OA and RA hyaline cartilage was assessed by direct ELISA. Immunofluorescent staining with anti-citrulline antibody was performed on histological sections of normal cartilage. Our results demonstrate significant reactivity to COL2 and three main COL2 epitopes, including citrullinated form of COL2 (358-369) epitope, in patients with OA. Collectively, more than 90% of the patients in the OA cohort showed reactivity against COL2 (358-369) epitope and/or citrullinated COL2 (358-369), which has not been observed in previous studies. A novel finding regarding COL2 citrullination of the present study is the determined tendency for higher relative level of citrullination of COL2 from arthritic patients compared to COL2 samples from individuals that do not suffer arthritic disorder. A tendency for increased relative anti-citrulline immunoreactivity for blood plasma proteins of RA patients compared to control individuals and OA patients was detected. Positive anti-citrulline staining was observed in the perichondrium and in the extracellular matrix surrounding chondrocytes in normal cartilage. Overall, our results indicate that citrullination is a physiological process that may become altered or enhanced during joint disease leading to bone destruction.

items.title: Co-Occurrence Patterns of Symptom and Functional Burden Associated with Tofacitinib and Upadacitinib: A Multidimensional Analysis of Spontaneous Reports in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pharmacovigilance studies typically evaluate adverse events as isolated drug-event pairs, potentially overlooking symptoms and functional impairments reported concurrently within the same case. We investigated co-reported adverse event patterns for tofacitinib and upadacitinib in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Methods: FAERS reports submitted between 2004 and 2025 were included if tofacitinib or upadacitinib was recorded as the primary suspect drug for RA. Disproportionality analysis was integrated with three co-occurrence network approaches, Bayesian network analysis, and time-to-onset (TTO) analysis. Methotrexate served as an indication-matched comparator. Network analyses were stratified by reporter and submission type, and TTO was reassessed for the common 2019-2025 period. FAERS signals were also compared descriptively with Canada Vigilance data. Results: We identified 57,438 tofacitinib-related and 29,869 upadacitinib-related reports, yielding 316 and 413 positive Preferred Term signals, respectively. In the tofacitinib networks, fatigue was consistently associated with pain, mood-related terms, treatment experience, and gastrointestinal and infectious events. Upadacitinib reports exhibited a distinct pattern, with falls, pain, functional limitations, and injuries occupying central positions. Reduced grip strength, decreased joint range of motion, and loss of personal independence formed a recurrent functional cluster. Methotrexate networks were primarily organized around disease-activity terms. The median reported TTO was 34 days for tofacitinib and 115 days for upadacitinib; corresponding values for the 2019-2025 period were 59 and 115 days, respectively. These intervals should not be interpreted as true onset latency or as established hazard patterns. Conclusions: Co-reporting analysis yielded insights beyond individual disproportionality signals. Tofacitinib reports were predominantly characterized by fatigue and associated symptoms, whereas upadacitinib reports more prominently featured functional limitations, falls, and injuries.

items.title: Composite Complete-Blood-Count-Derived Inflammatory Indices for Discriminating Established Major Organ Involvement in Behçet's Disease: A Cross-Sectional Nomogram Model.
items.abstract: Introduction : Differentiating major organ involvement (MOI) from isolated mucocutaneous manifestations in Behçet's disease (BD) remains a substantial clinical challenge, particularly in stable outpatients outside acute flares. This study aimed to evaluate the cross-sectional discriminatory utility of complete blood count (CBC)-derived composite inflammatory indices-specifically the Systemic Inflammatory Response Index (SIRI), Systemic Immuno-Inflammatory Index (SII), and Aggregate Index of Systemic Inflammation (AISI)-and to construct an internally validated diagnostic nomogram. Methods : A total of 178 BD patients (88 with established MOI and 90 with isolated mucocutaneous involvement) classified according to the 2014 International Criteria for Behçet's Disease (ICBD) were included in this cross-sectional study. Concurrently measured hematological parameters, acute-phase reactants (Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate [ESR] and C-Reactive Protein [CRP]), and ongoing therapies were analyzed. Discriminative performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Independent indicators of MOI were identified via multivariable Firth's penalized logistic regression, and a nomogram was generated with 1000-sample bootstrap internal validation. Results : In the MOI group, SIRI, SII, and AISI levels were statistically significantly higher than in the mucocutaneous group ( p < 0.001); in contrast, no statistically significant difference was observed in ESR and CRP levels ( p > 0.05). SIRI provided the highest numerical point estimate for AUC (0.919, 95% CI: 0.880-0.956); however, formal matched ROC comparisons showed that SIRI's discriminatory performance was statistically comparable to that of AISI (AUC: 0.916; p = 0.800) and SII (AUC: 0.889; p = 0.211). In a multivariable analysis adjusted for age, sex, and duration of illness, SIRI remained strongly and independently associated with MOI (adjusted OR: 90.19, 95% CI: 22.20-366.44, p < 0.001). The SIRI-based diagnostic nomogram demonstrated robust calibration and discriminatory power (optimism-adjusted AUC = 0.912, Brier score = 0.115). Conclusions : Conventional acute-phase reactants fail to reflect established MOI in BD patients receiving maintenance therapies outside acute flares. In contrast, composite CBC-derived indices-SIRI, SII and AISI-exhibit strong discriminative accuracy. The internally validated nomogram provides an accessible clinical stratification tool. However, the present cross-sectional data do not establish prediction of future MOI, prognosis, or subclinical vasculitis.

items.title: Circulating suPAR in Relation to Renal and Cardiovascular Involvement in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Pilot Study.
items.abstract: Soluble urokinase plasminogen activator receptor (suPAR) is an inflammatory biomarker associated with immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, and chronic inflammation. Increasing evidence suggests that suPAR may be involved in renal and cardiovascular injury and may reflect cumulative organ damage in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Serum suPAR levels were measured in patients with SLE and healthy controls. Within the SLE cohort, suPAR levels were further evaluated according to the presence or absence of organ involvement. In this pilot study, serum suPAR levels were significantly higher in patients with SLE than in healthy controls. Within the SLE cohort, patients with renal involvement and those with reduced renal function had higher suPAR levels than their respective comparison groups. Similarly, patients with cardiovascular involvement showed significantly higher suPAR levels than SLE patients without cardiovascular involvement and healthy controls. However, serum suPAR levels were not significantly correlated with estimated glomerular filtration rate. Circulating suPAR levels are elevated in SLE and may be particularly associated with renal and cardiovascular involvement. These findings support the potential role of suPAR as a biomarker of cardiorenal involvement in SLE, although its relationship with renal function and clinical outcomes requires validation in larger prospective cohorts.

items.title: Donor-Resolved Analysis of HES1-Associated Fibroblast States in Systemic Sclerosis.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: We examined HES1-associated fibroblast states in systemic sclerosis (SSc) and the rationale for testing upstream γ-secretase inhibition with nirogacestat. Methods: We analysed 325,636 skin cells from 230 donors across five non-redundant cohorts using complete computational transcription-factor screens, donor-level activity and trajectory analyses, multiome data and spatial assays. Donors or independent simulations were the inference units, with cohort adjustment and multiplicity correction where applicable. Three independent 200 ns molecular dynamics runs per condition compared nirogacestat-bound and ligand-deleted γ-secretase models. Results: HES1 activity was positively associated with model-derived myofibroblast fate in 98.1% of 206 donors (median Spearman's ρ=0.282; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.258-0.309). The adjusted SSc-healthy control activity difference was uncertain (0.21; 95% CI, -0.01 to 0.43; Benjamini-Hochberg q=0.061). HES1 ranked 28/107 and 30/109 in the descriptive screens; SMAD3 showed a stronger association with cell fate. Disease-specific communication and contact-enrichment tests did not provide statistical support. The adjusted Visium association was negative; Xenium showed a weak positive mean without section-level corrected support. Nirogacestat was selected retrospectively through mechanistic and translational evidence despite a weak expression-reversal signal and discordant tofacitinib-signature alignment. Simulations showed lower reference-defined pocket root mean square deviation (RMSD) in bound models, with substantial sampling and endpoint-energy uncertainty. Conclusions: HES1 activity marks a consistent fibroblast-state association, with uncertain causality and SSc specificity. Nirogacestat is a candidate compound for experimental testing of upstream Notch-pathway perturbation in SSc fibroblasts; the computational findings do not establish efficacy.

items.title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Single-Cell Analysis Reveals Shared Macrophage-Associated Inflammatory Signatures in MASLD/NAFLD and Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease/nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (MASLD/NAFLD) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) may share inflammatory mechanisms, although their common cellular basis remains unclear. We integrated bulk transcriptomic datasets (GSE66676 and GSE55235), single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets from murine RA synovium (GSE192504) and NASH liver (GSE129516), disease-association analysis, molecular docking, and in vitro experiments in LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages. Bulk transcriptomic analysis identified 630 shared differentially expressed genes, including 344 concordantly upregulated genes enriched in immune response, cytokine and chemokine signaling, phagosome, Toll-like receptor signaling, and Fc receptor-mediated phagocytosis; a strict dual-dataset intersection further defined 18 core genes significantly upregulated in both diseases. Immune-signature analysis indicated altered myeloid cell-associated inflammatory activity in both diseases, and several shared genes, including S100A8, S100A9, FCER1G, FCGR3A, LYZ, and MS4A7, correlated positively with monocyte/macrophage-related signatures. Single-cell analysis identified macrophage subsets with high S100a9 expression and elevated shared myeloid inflammatory signature scores in both RA synovium and NASH liver. Triptolide showed favorable predicted binding to the S100A8/A9 complex and reduced LPS-induced inflammatory cytokine secretion and expression of the six-gene signature in RAW264.7 cells, supporting the hypothesis that S100A9-associated inflammatory macrophage activation represents a candidate target for further investigation. These findings support a shared S100A9-positive inflammatory macrophage-associated program in MASLD/NAFLD and RA, and support the hypothesis that the S100A8/A9 complex represents a candidate target for further investigation.

items.title: Clinical Phenotype, Treatment Exposure, Treat-to-Target Status, and Longitudinal Outcomes in Juvenile-Onset Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Treat-to-target assessment is central to the management of juvenile-onset systemic lupus erythematosus (jSLE). We primarily evaluated last-visit childhood lupus low disease activity state (cLLDAS) status and its limiting components, and secondarily described clinical phenotype, treatment exposure, and outcomes. Methods: This retrospective single-center cohort included 54 patients with jSLE followed during 2020-2025; one patient who died 10 days after diagnosis was excluded from last-visit analyses, and the remaining 53 had at least 6 months of follow-up. The Paediatric Rheumatology European Society (PReS)-endorsed cLLDAS definition was applied at the last visit using a retrospectively assigned physician global assessment (PGA). Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Disease Activity Index 2000 (SLEDAI-2K) and laboratory values at diagnosis and the latest assessment were compared descriptively. Results: Median age at diagnosis was 15.0 years, and median follow-up was 34.6 months (IQR 21.2-70.6). Biopsy-proven lupus nephritis occurred in 29.6% (class IV, 13/16). Median SLEDAI-2K was 8.0 at diagnosis and 4.0 at the latest assessment. At the last visit, 29/53 patients (54.7%; 95% CI 40.4-68.4) were in cLLDAS, and 32/53 (60.4%) met the SLEDAI-2K and glucocorticoid components; of 24 patients outside the target, 17 had SLEDAI-2K > 4 and 7 exceeded the glucocorticoid ceiling (both in 3). Conservative minimum rates of flare, infection-related hospitalization, and intensive care unit admission were 5.6, 5.2, and 1.4 per 100 patient-years, respectively; one early death occurred. Conclusions: Just over half of the patients were in cLLDAS at the last visit, with residual disease activity as the main barrier, followed by glucocorticoid dose. These observational data reflect outcomes within the available follow-up period and cannot establish treatment effectiveness or long-term prognosis.

items.title: Sexual Function After Corrective Spinal Osteotomy in Female Patients with Ankylosing Spondylitis: A Retrospective Single-Center Case Series.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) may cause progressive spinal rigidity and kyphotic deformity, with consequences for physical function, quality of life, and sexual health. Data regarding sexual function following corrective spinal osteotomy in women with AS are limited. This study aimed to describe radiological and functional changes and to explore within-patient changes in sexual function following corrective spinal osteotomy. Methods: This retrospective single-center case series analyzed prospectively maintained data from female patients with AS who underwent single-level pedicle subtraction osteotomy for thoracolumbar kyphosis between 2015 and 2024. The primary outcome was the change in total Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI) score from baseline to the standardized two-year assessment. Secondary outcomes (analyzed as exploratory, without adjustment for multiplicity) included FSFI domains, Visual Analog Scale, Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Functional Index, and radiological parameters. Sexual-activity frequency, time to resumption of sexual activity, and preferred coital position were also recorded. Paired outcomes were analyzed using the exact Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and exploratory radiological-FSFI associations using Spearman's correlation with false-discovery-rate adjustment. Results: Eleven patients with complete two-year data were included. Significant postoperative changes were observed in several sagittal alignment parameters, as well as in Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Functional Index (BASFI) scores. Total FSFI and the desire, arousal, orgasm, and satisfaction domains increased, whereas lubrication and pain did not change significantly. A descriptive shift toward higher-frequency sexual activity and different preferred coital positions was also observed. Radiological-FSFI correlations were interpreted cautiously because of the small sample and multiple comparisons. Conclusions: In this small exploratory cohort, postoperative assessment was associated with improved radiological alignment, pain, physical function, and several domains of self-reported sexual function. These findings represent within-patient changes and exploratory associations and do not establish a causal effect of spinal osteotomy on sexual function or a specific safe interval for resumption of sexual activity. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm these observations.

items.title: Area-Level Rurality and Documented Musculoskeletal Symptom Presentation at Rheumatoid Arthritis Diagnosis Among Older Adults in Rural Japan: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: Background: Recognizing rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in older adults is challenging because clinical presentations are heterogeneous and musculoskeletal symptoms may be attributed to aging or other conditions. Rural context may influence symptom recognition, healthcare-seeking, and diagnostic pathways. We examined whether area-level rurality was associated with musculoskeletal symptoms documented at RA diagnosis among older adults in rural Japan. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 221 patients aged ≥65 years diagnosed with RA at a rural community hospital in Japan between 2016 and 2021. Area-level rurality was measured using the Rurality Index for Japan (RIJ). The primary outcome was documentation of hand, wrist, foot, or ankle symptoms at diagnosis. Logistic regression was used to examine the association between RIJ and the primary outcome. The primary adjusted model included age, sex, and Charlson Comorbidity Index. Results: Among 221 patients, 106 (48.0%) had documented hand, wrist, foot, or ankle symptoms. RIJ scores were higher among patients with these documented symptoms than among those without them (70.0 vs. 64.8; p = 0.004), and the interval from symptom onset to the study-hospital consultation was longer (48.5 vs. 28.0 days; p < 0.001). Each 10-point increase in RIJ was associated with higher odds of documented hand, wrist, foot, or ankle symptoms in the primary adjusted model (OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.07-1.57; p = 0.008). Exploratory sequential models incorporating consultation timing, CRP, and anti-CCP antibody levels yielded similar estimates. Sensitivity analysis accounting for clustering by residential postal-code area did not materially alter the association. Conclusions: Greater area-level rurality was modestly associated with the joint symptom pattern documented at RA diagnosis among older adults in this rural healthcare system. The findings should be interpreted as reflecting differences in documented clinical presentation within a diagnostic pathway rather than as evidence of a distinct rural RA phenotype. In rural settings, clinicians should systematically assess musculoskeletal symptoms in older adults with suspected inflammatory arthritis while remaining attentive to atypical presentations. Prospective multicenter studies using standardized joint assessments and direct individual-level measures of healthcare accessibility are needed to clarify how rural context relates to symptom recognition, healthcare-seeking, referral, and RA diagnosis.

items.title: Exploratory Risk Assessment of Cardiovascular Diseases Using Antiphospholipid Antibody-Related Scores in Patients with ANCA-Associated Vasculitis.
items.abstract: Background: Antiphospholipid antibodies have been found in patients with antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (AAV). This study aimed to evaluate the accuracy of the global antiphospholipid syndrome score (GAPSS) derivatives in predicting cardiovascular diseases in Korean patients with AAV, and to derive a simple candidate index for cardiovascular diseases. Methods: This was a retrospective cohort study including 170 patients with AAV. The adjusted GAPSS (aGAPSS), aGAPSS specific for cardiovascular diseases (aGAPSScvd), and aGAPSS for Korean patients with APS (aGAPSS [KAPS]) were calculated in each patient. The cardiovascular diseases were defined as cerebrovascular accident (CVA) or acute coronary syndrome (ACS). The accuracy of each index was assessed by estimating the area under the curve (AUC). An exploratory multivariable Cox proportional hazards model with a backward elimination method was performed to derive a candidate index. Covariates consisting the aGAPSScvd were included in the model. Results: The AUCs of the aGAPSS, aGAPSScvd, and aGAPSS (KAPS) for CVA were 0.507 ( p = 0.926), 0.531 ( p = 0.676), and 0.493 ( p = 0.923), respectively. The AUCs of the aGAPSS, aGAPSScvd, and aGAPSS (KAPS) for ACS were 0.613 ( p = 0.441), 0.752 ( p = 0.086), and 0.796 ( p = 0.043), respectively. The exploratory multivariable model revealed a candidate index, aGAPSScvd for ACS in Korean patients with AAV (aGAPSScvd [KAAV]) = 2 × lupus anticoagulant (LA) + 2 × obesity. The AUC of the aGAPSScvd (KAAV) in predicting ACS was 0.843 ( p = 0.019). Conclusions: The two-item candidate index aGAPSScvd (KAAV), consisting of LA and obesity, showed discriminatory ability for ACS, which warrants further validation in larger studies.

items.title: Association of Anti-TNF Therapy with Ventricular Repolarization Indices in Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Longitudinal Electrocardiographic Study.
items.abstract: Background: Patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) have an increased risk of cardiovascular morbidity that cannot be fully explained by traditional cardiovascular risk factors alone. Chronic systemic inflammation has been implicated in myocardial electrical remodeling, yet the effect of anti-tumor necrosis factor (anti-TNF) therapy on ventricular repolarization remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigated longitudinal changes in electrocardiographic markers of ventricular repolarization following anti-TNF therapy in patients with RA. Methods: This retrospective longitudinal study included 115 patients with RA who initiated anti-TNF therapy and had clinical, laboratory, and 12-lead electrocardiographic assessments at baseline and after approximately 24 weeks. Ventricular repolarization was evaluated using QT, corrected QT (QTc), Tpeak-Tend (Tp-e), corrected Tp-e (cTp-e), and Tp-e/QT. Cross-sectional associations between repolarization indices and inflammatory/disease-related variables were assessed at 24 weeks, together with longitudinal correlations between changes in these variables and changes in repolarization indices. Results: The mean age was 54.4 ± 12.2 years, and 81.7% of participants were women. After 24 weeks of treatment, significant reductions were observed in CRP, ESR, DAS28-CRP, and HAQ scores (all p < 0.001). The Tp-e interval decreased from 85.1 ± 13.6 to 75.3 ± 13.5 ms, and the Tp-e/QT ratio decreased from 0.20 ± 0.04 to 0.18 ± 0.03 (both p < 0.001), with moderate within-subject effect sizes for both changes (Cohen's dz = 0.46). At 24 weeks, Tp-e and Tp-e/QT were positively correlated with inflammatory markers, disease activity, functional impairment, and disease duration. However, longitudinal change-to-change analyses showed no consistent associations between changes in inflammatory/disease activity measures and changes in repolarization indices, except for a weak correlation between ΔDAS28-CRP and ΔTp-e ( r = 0.201, p = 0.031). Despite a significant reduction in mean QTc, the proportion of patients with prolonged QTc remained unchanged (18.3% at both assessments; McNemar p = 1.00). Conclusions: Anti-TNF therapy in patients with RA was associated with significant improvements in several ECG-derived ventricular repolarization indices alongside reductions in inflammatory and disease activity. However, the lack of consistent longitudinal correlations and the unchanged prevalence of prolonged QTc indicate that these findings should be interpreted as treatment-associated changes rather than evidence of a direct electrophysiological or antiarrhythmic effect of TNF inhibition. Prospective controlled studies incorporating clinical cardiovascular outcomes are warranted.

items.title: Complete Blood Count-Derived Inflammatory Indices Following Whole-Body Cryotherapy Combined with Kinesiotherapy Versus Kinesiotherapy Alone in Men with Ankylosing Spondylitis.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: The response of complete blood count (CBC)-derived inflammatory indices to whole-body cryotherapy (WBC) in ankylosing spondylitis (AS) remains unknown. This exploratory post hoc secondary analysis examined whether adding WBC to kinesiotherapy was associated with differences in these indices and explored their associations with disease activity, pain, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) levels. Prospectively collected data from 32 men with AS were analyzed. Participants were allocated by alternation, rather than randomization, to WBC combined with kinesiotherapy (WBC + K; n = 16) or kinesiotherapy alone (KT; n = 16). Methods: Prospectively collected data from 32 men with ankylosing spondylitis (AS) who participated in a prior study were analyzed. Participants were allocated to whole-body cryotherapy combined with kinesiotherapy (WBC + K; n = 16) or kinesiotherapy alone (KT; n = 16). Complete blood count parameters, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) levels, Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index (BASDAI), and visual analogue scale (VAS) pain scores were assessed prospectively before and after the intervention. Previously unpublished complete blood count data were used to calculate the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) post hoc and to explore their associations with hsCRP, BASDAI, and VAS pain. The primary intervention effects were assessed using baseline-adjusted analysis of covariance, and the five treatment-effect p -values were subjected to Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Comparisons of changes from baseline were performed as sensitivity analyses. Results: None of the baseline-adjusted between-group treatment effects for NLR, PLR, MLR, SII, or SIRI were statistically significant before or after false discovery rate correction. The adjusted between-group difference for MLR was -0.033 (95% confidence interval: -0.074 to 0.008; p = 0.115; q = 0.329). In the change-score sensitivity analysis, the between-group difference in MLR change was nominally significant ( p = 0.012) but did not meet the multiplicity-adjusted significance threshold ( q = 0.060). Within the WBC + K group, PLR, MLR, and SIRI decreased significantly, whereas no corresponding within-group changes were observed in the KT group; however, these within-group findings were descriptive and did not establish an additional effect of WBC. Changes in the indices were not significantly correlated with changes in hsCRP, BASDAI, or VAS pain. None of the exploratory post-treatment correlations remained significant after multiple-testing correction. Conclusions: This study did not provide baseline-adjusted or multiplicity-adjusted evidence that adding WBC to kinesiotherapy affected any of the investigated CBC-derived inflammatory indices in men with AS. The nominal MLR signal identified in the change-score sensitivity analysis and the within-group reductions in PLR, MLR, and SIRI should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Larger, prospectively designed, adequately powered randomized studies with prespecified outcomes and baseline-adjusted analyses are required.

items.title: Host-Microbe Crosstalk in Sjögren's Disease: Epithelial Type I Interferon Amplification, Loss of Short-Chain Fatty Acid Restraint, and the Effector-Phase Focus of Validated Therapy.
items.abstract: Sjögren's disease (SjD) is a systemic autoimmune disease of the exocrine glands, long framed as a lymphocyte-driven disorder in which immune cells destroy the target tissue. Genomic, epigenetic, microbiome, and single-cell and spatial studies have since shown the glandular epithelium and the microbial environment to be active participants rather than passive bystanders. This review asks whether host susceptibility and microbiome change can be joined into one continuous axis, following it from genetic and epigenetic susceptibility, through microbiome change read functionally rather than taxonomically, to the crosstalk that converts microbial signals into a host response and the cell states carrying it in human tissue. Two axes run through the whole sequence: the type I interferon (IFN) response and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) metabolism. Read against them, every disease-modifying therapy with validated efficacy so far acts in the downstream B-cell effector axis, whereas the upstream IFN axis has yielded no established treatment. Because the microbial layer and the salivary gland transcriptome or proteome have never been measured in the same patients, the model proposed here remains a testable hypothesis rather than a completed causal chain. The aim is to specify that model, the falsification conditions it carries, and the study design its verification requires.

items.title: Preclinical Mouse Models of Rheumatoid Arthritis: Comparative Insights into Inflammatory Mediators and Immune Cells.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent synovial inflammation, progressive cartilage destruction, and bone erosion. Mouse models are essential for investigating RA pathogenesis, defining immune-cell and cytokine networks, and evaluating potential therapies. Common models include collagen-induced arthritis (CIA), collagen antibody-induced arthritis (CAIA), human TNF transgenic (hTNF-Tg) arthritis, and SKG arthritis, each representing distinct inflammatory mechanisms. CIA involves adaptive and innate immune cells, including CD4 + T cells, B cells, dendritic cells, macrophages, and neutrophils, with prominent roles for TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-17A, GM-CSF, and IL-23. CAIA primarily reflects antibody-mediated and innate immune mechanisms involving neutrophils, macrophages, complement, and Fcγ receptors, with contributions from TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, GM-CSF, CXCL1, and CXCL2. The hTNF-Tg model highlights chronic TNF-driven inflammation involving macrophages and neutrophils and downstream inflammatory mediators such as IL-1β, IL-6, CXCL1, and CCL2. In contrast, the SKG model emphasizes autoreactive CD4 + T-cell and Th17 responses, with IL-17A, IL-6, and IL-23 contributing to arthritis following environmental stimulation. Collectively, these models are mechanistically complementary and provide distinct insights into immune activation, cytokine signaling, and joint pathology. However, differences in immune regulation, disease heterogeneity, and inflammatory mechanisms between mice and humans emphasize the importance of careful model selection and interpretation. This review summarizes major mouse models of RA, focusing on their immune-cell and inflammatory mediator networks, therapeutic applications, and translational relevance to human disease.

items.title: Positivity Rates and Serum Levels of Antibodies Against Histone H3 Lysine 9 and Its Lactylated Form in Rheumatoid Arthritis and Its Mimics.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives : To compare the positivity rates and serum levels of antibodies against histone H3 lysine 9 (anti-H3K9) and its lactylated form (anti-H3K9la) among patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), or Sjögren disease (SjD) and controls. Methods : Serum anti-H3K9 and anti-H3K9la levels were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay from 93 patients with RA, 40 with SLE, 40 with SjD, and 40 controls. Antibody findings were compared across study groups and according to rheumatoid factor immunoglobulin M (RF-IgM) and anti-citrullinated protein antibody (ACPA) status in RA. Results: Anti-H3K9 positivity was 28.0% in RA, 40.0% in SLE, 0% in SjD, and 2.5% in controls. Anti-H3K9la positivity was 22.6% in RA and 20.0% in SLE; no SjD patients or controls were positive. Patients with SjD had lower levels of both antibodies than controls. No statistically significant differences were detected according to RF-IgM or ACPA status, although the seronegative subgroups were small. In exploratory multivariable models, TNF inhibitor use was associated with higher levels of both antibodies. Adding either antibody to ACPA and RF-IgM increased sensitivity at the expense of specificity. Conclusions: Anti-H3K9 and anti-H3K9la antibodies were detected more frequently in RA and SLE than in controls, whereas patients with SjD had lower serum levels of both antibodies. No statistically significant differences in antibody positivity or levels were detected according to RF-IgM or ACPA status in RA, although the small seronegative subgroups limited the precision of these comparisons. Their potential value as adjunctive diagnostic biomarkers requires confirmation in larger, independent cohorts with formal diagnostic-performance analyses.
